items.title: Priority tiers misread clusters with their own PriorityClasses: "critical" can rank below normal, and Homestead can make itself evictable
items.body:
**Homestead version:** 2.8.324 · k3s v1.37.1

**Extends earlier work:** the priority tiers I added in #410 (part of #347), which #415 then extended to VMs and to protecting Homestead itself. This is a gap in that work: it assumed Homestead's own classes are the only ones on the cluster.

## Summary

Homestead works out an app's tier from the **name** of its PriorityClass: `homestead-critical`, `homestead-low`, or no class. It never reads a class's **value**, and never checks which class is the cluster's default.

A cluster with its own classes is common: Flux and Helm users, charts with their own class, a cluster-wide default. On such a cluster, Homestead misreads the ranking. In some cases it also makes it worse: "critical" ranks below normal, and Homestead puts itself where any app can evict it.

The wiki already promises the right thing ("normal… means that class" on a cluster with a default, Containers → Priority tiers). The code doesn't follow it yet.

## How the ranking works (for reference)

From the Kubernetes docs and the admission plugin source:
- **A pod's priority is a number.** It comes from its class's `value`, resolved once, when the pod is created. Higher means more important.
- **One class may be the `globalDefault`.** A pod that names no class gets that class's **name and value**; with no default, it gets 0.
- **Neither can change later:** not a pod's priority, and not a class's value. Re-ranking means recreating pods.
- **The scheduler preempts by number:** a pending pod can evict only pods with a lower number.

## What Homestead does

- **`homestead_priority.tier_of()`** maps `homestead-critical` / `homestead-low` / `homestead-normal` / no class to tiers, by name. Any other class is "other".
- **The forecast** (`homestead_capacity.forecast()`, which reads pods) places "other" with normal.
- **`ensure()`** creates `homestead-critical` at **1000** and `homestead-low` at **-1000**, neither as default. If a class of that name already exists with another value, it's kept with a note.
- **`protect()`** runs every minute on the leader. When any pod uses `homestead-critical` and no job is running, it moves Homestead into `homestead-critical` without comparing values. It leaves Homestead alone if its template already names a class.
- **Other users of the tier:** the reservation suggestions use it too. Critical apps get extra memory headroom.

## What goes wrong

Take a cluster with its own classes: `x-critical` 100000, `x-normal` 10000 marked **globalDefault**, `x-low` 1000 with `preemptionPolicy: Never`. That's a usual three-tier setup, and how my own cluster is configured.

1. **The forecast is wrong.** The default gives every pod the class's name as well as its value, so every pod reads as "other" and is counted as normal. Apps on `x-critical` and `x-low` lose their rank in "If this host goes down", and an app on `homestead-critical` (1000) is counted above `x-critical` ones (100000).
2. **"Critical" ranks below normal.** An app or VM set to critical in Homestead gets `homestead-critical` at 1000. That's below every pod on the default (10000), and equal to the cluster's own low tier. Every ordinary pod outranks the "critical" app and can evict it.
3. **Homestead makes itself evictable.** Once anything uses `homestead-critical`, `protect()` moves Homestead from the default's 10000 down to 1000. That's the opposite of #415's "no critical app can evict Homestead": here every normal app can.
4. **The cluster's own tiers can't be used.** Apps whose template names `x-critical` or `x-low` show as "other": Priority tiers skips them, and Edit makes them read-only. So do the extra memory headroom for critical apps and the rest of Homestead's tier-aware behaviour.
5. **A clashing class is kept without warning.** A class's value can't be changed after it's created. If `homestead-critical` already exists at another value, the mismatch stays for good.

## Also in this area: changes that get undone

- **Edit changes tiers on apps Homestead doesn't own.** The bulk Priority tiers list refuses apps that Flux or Argo CD apply, and says "set priorityClassName there". Edit has no such check (`homestead_lifecycle._apply_priority`, `homestead_workloads`), so a tier set there is reverted at the next sync. Edit should behave like the list.
- **Plain Helm installs aren't recognised as owned elsewhere.** `homestead_updates.managed_by` doesn't check them, so the next `helm upgrade` undoes a change. Homestead's own install is a Helm release (`charts/homestead`), and `managed_by` also decides what the image-updates page offers. So any Helm check has to exclude Homestead itself.

## What a person should get (no new settings)

- **Nothing to set up.** Homestead reads the cluster's classes (name, value, default, preemption) and the **priority number on each pod**, and ranks by number. A cluster with no PriorityClasses at all behaves exactly as today.
- **Critical, normal and low keep their meaning,** by this rule:
  - **Normal** is the cluster's default class, or 0 without one.
  - **Critical** is the highest class above the default that may preempt, excluding `system-*` classes. If there is none, Homestead creates one between the default and 1,000,000,000 under a **new** name (an existing `homestead-critical` can't be changed).
  - **Low** is a class below the default, preferably one that never preempts. If there is none, Homestead creates one.
  - **If it can't decide,** for example the default is at the cap or two classes tie, it warns rather than guessing.
- **Homestead protects itself by number.** It joins a class at least as high as the highest app tier, and never one below the default. It marks the class it set itself (say, an annotation), so it can move itself up later. A class a person gave it is still left alone.
- **Existing clusters are fixed.** One where Homestead already sits in `homestead-critical` at 1000 below a higher default is moved up once, with the same restart `protect()` already does.
- **The forecast, the reservation suggestions, and the capacity check shown before a move or edit** all use the pods' real numbers.
- **Warnings only when something is actually wrong:**
  - a "critical" class ranked at or below the default;
  - a class that apps reference but that doesn't exist (their new pods are refused);
  - Homestead ranked below an app it should outrank.

**Workaround until then:** give Homestead's own Deployment a class yourself, such as your cluster's critical one, and `protect()` leaves it alone.

## Related, possibly a separate issue

From reading the code (`homestead_self_data_bootstrap.py:114-124`), not reproduced: a data-move helper pod is held if admission adds fields outside its allow-list or sets `priority != 0`. A cluster default adds both (`priorityClassName`, and its value), so on such a cluster those helper pods would likely be held with "Admission added unreviewed helper pod settings". Happy to split this out if you prefer.

I'm happy to send a PR for this.

items.title: Bug: v1.6's delete-protection finalizer is never removed from migrated TemporalWorkerDeployment/TemporalConnection, so they stay Terminating after the v1.7 migration
items.body:
### Summary

After migrating from v1.6 to v1.7 (`TemporalWorkerDeployment` → `WorkerDeployment`, `TemporalConnection` → `Connection`), the old objects stay in `Terminating` forever. The migration itself succeeds: the new `WorkerDeployment` adopts the Deployments, the old object is labelled migrated, and the deprecated reconciler releases `temporal.io/migration-guard`. But the old objects still carry the `temporal.io/delete-protection` finalizer that v1.6 added, and nothing in v1.7+ ever removes it from the deprecated kinds.

### Versions

- Controller: v1.6.0 (chart 0.25.0) → v1.7.1 (chart 0.28.1), CRDs chart upgraded first as documented. The same code is still present in v1.12.0.
- Applied with GitOps (Argo CD); same steps as [docs/migration-crd-rename.md](https://github.com/temporalio/temporal-worker-controller/blob/main/docs/migration-crd-rename.md) Step 3: the manifests change kind, so the old objects are deleted and the new ones created in one sync.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Run v1.6.0 with a `TemporalWorkerDeployment` and a `TemporalConnection`. v1.6's `WorkerDeploymentReconciler` adds `temporal.io/delete-protection` to both (`worker_controller.go`, `finalizerName`).
2. Upgrade the CRDs, then the controller to v1.7.x.
3. Replace the manifests with `WorkerDeployment` / `Connection` of the same names (this deletes the old objects).

### Expected

Per the migration guide: "The migration-guard finalizer holds each deprecated resource in `Terminating` state until the controller confirms ownership transfer is complete, then removes the finalizer and lets the deletion finish."

### Actual

The `WorkerDeployment`s and `Connection` reconcile and the workers keep running on the new objects, but the old objects never finish deleting:

```
$ kubectl get temporalworkerdeployment <name> -o jsonpath='{.metadata.finalizers}'
["temporal.io/delete-protection"]
```

`migration-guard` is gone (the migrated label is set), and only `delete-protection` remains. For an Argo CD application this blocks the sync: the old objects never go away, so the app stays out of sync and a release that waits on it times out.

### Cause

From v1.7 the deprecated kinds are handled by `DeprecatedTWDReconciler` / `DeprecatedTCReconciler`, which only add and remove `temporal.io/migration-guard`. The comment in `deprecated_reconciler.go` says that is deliberate ("intentionally distinct from the existing `temporal.io/delete-protection` finalizer, which lives on WorkerDeployment/Connection"). That reasoning holds for objects created after v1.7. But every object that existed under v1.6 already carries `delete-protection`, and since the `WorkerDeploymentReconciler` no longer reconciles the old kinds, nothing removes it.

### Workaround

Once migration is confirmed, remove the leftover finalizer, guarded so that it only acts when `delete-protection` is the last finalizer left (that is, after `migration-guard` was released):

```
kubectl -n <ns> patch temporalworkerdeployment <name> --type=json -p='[
  {"op":"test","path":"/metadata/finalizers","value":["temporal.io/delete-protection"]},
  {"op":"remove","path":"/metadata/finalizers"}]'
```

Same for `temporalconnection`. This made no Temporal API call: the server-side Worker Deployment stays owned by the new `WorkerDeployment`, and the Kubernetes Deployments (owned only by the new object by then) are untouched.

### Suggested fix

When the deprecated reconcilers release `migration-guard` on a migrated object, also remove `temporal.io/delete-protection` from it. The new `WorkerDeployment` / `Connection` already owns the server-side cleanup that finalizer was for, so this cleanup must not run for the old object. Alternatively, document the step in the migration guide, in the same way the downgrade guide already covers re-adding `delete-protection`.

items.title: bug(compiler): invalid literal for int() crash when compiling dsl.If condition comparing numeric channel to boolean
items.body:
## Summary
Compiling a pipeline that uses `dsl.If` (or its deprecated alias `dsl.Condition`) to compare a **numeric** `PipelineChannel` (an `int` or `float` task output) against a **boolean literal** (`True`/`False`) crashes the compiler with an unhandled `ValueError`, instead of either compiling correctly or failing with a clear validation error.

## Current behavior
```python
from kfp import dsl
from kfp import compiler

@dsl.component
def comp() -> int:
    return 1

@dsl.component
def print_msg(msg: str):
    print(msg)

@dsl.pipeline
def my_pipe():
    t = comp()
    with dsl.If(t.output == True):
        print_msg(msg='hello')

compiler.Compiler().compile(my_pipe, 'pipe.yaml')
```
## Actual error

When compiling the pipeline, the compiler raises a `ValueError`:

```text
ValueError: invalid literal for int() with base 10: "int(inputs.parameter_values['pipelinechannel--comp-Output'])"
```
## Root cause

In `sdk/python/kfp/compiler/pipeline_spec_builder.py`, the function `_single_binary_operation_to_cel_condition` attempts to convert an operand to a Python integer using `int(operand_value)`.

However, when the operand comes from a `PipelineChannel`, `operand_value` can be a string representing a CEL expression rather than an actual numeric value.

For example:

```python
int("int(inputs.parameter_values['pipelinechannel--comp-Output'])")
```

Python cannot convert this expression string into an integer, so compilation fails with a `ValueError`.

The same line also appears to have inverted boolean conversion logic: zero maps to `true`, while non-zero values map to `false`. A fix should address both issues.



## Confirmed scope (tested variants)

The following cases were reproduced with the same compiler error:

- `t.output == True` and `True == t.output` (both operand orders).
- `t.output == False`.
- `t.output != True`.
- A float-typed channel compared with `True`.
- `dsl.Condition(...)`, the deprecated alias of `dsl.If`.

The issue occurs during condition compilation in the `dsl.If`/`dsl.Condition` path.


## Suggested fix approach

- Distinguish concrete numeric constants from symbolic CEL expressions generated from `PipelineChannel` objects.
- Avoid converting CEL expression strings to Python integers.
- Correct the inverted boolean mapping so that zero maps to `false` and non-zero values map to `true`, where this conversion is intended.
- Add regression tests for numeric-channel comparisons with `True` and `False`, covering both operand orders and the `!=` operator.

## Workaround

Compare the numeric channel with a numeric literal instead of a boolean literal, if that matches the intended logic. For example:

```python
with dsl.If(t.output == 1):
    print_msg(msg='hello')
```


/kind bug
/area compiler

items.body:
We deployed the `docs` chart from `main` (commit `24ae7b7ec91b`) with the
`ghcr.io/euro-office/cluster-docs` and `cluster-utils` images at
`v9.3.4-hotfix.1`, using external PostgreSQL, Redis and RabbitMQ. It runs now,
but only after working around the following. Each one stopped the install.
Happy to send PRs if they're welcome.

### 1. The default image tag doesn't exist

`values.yaml` sets `images.tag: 9.3.1-1`. ghcr has `v9.3.1` … `v9.3.4`,
`v9.3.4-hotfix.1`, `latest` and `nightly`, but no `9.3.1-1`, so a default
install fails with ImagePullBackOff. The tag has to be set explicitly.

### 2. Pods crash on `/etc//documentserver/...`

The image sets `COMPANY_NAME_LOW` but not `COMPANY_NAME`, and the startup
scripts build paths from `COMPANY_NAME`, so they come out as
`/etc//documentserver/...`. Workaround: `COMPANY_NAME=euro-office` via
`extraEnvVars`.

### 3. The schema hook loads an empty file and reports success

The DB init hook downloads the schema from
`ONLYOFFICE/server/master/...`, which now returns 404. The 404 body is loaded
as the schema "successfully", the database stays empty, and docservice then
fails on missing tables (`doc_changes`, `task_result`). Workaround:
`privateCluster: true` with our own `init-db-scripts` / `remove-db-scripts`
ConfigMaps built from `euro-office/server@56bc9d4`. The hook should probably
fetch from `euro-office/server`, and fail on a non-200 response.

### 4. RabbitMQ vhost naming

With a dedicated vhost, the docs and defaults disagree on the name
(`euro-office` vs `/euro-office`), and the AMQP URL then points at a vhost
that doesn't exist (`vhost euro-office not found`).

### 5. `amqpVhost` is concatenated without a separator

The chart builds the AMQP URL as `host:port` + `amqpVhost`. With
`amqpVhost: euro-office` that gives
`ENOTFOUND rabbitmq-client...:5672euro-office`. It only works when
`amqpVhost` starts with `/` (`/euro-office`), which then names the vhost
`euro-office`. Either the template should add the `/`, or the values
documentation should say it's required.

---

Environment: Kubernetes 1.33, Flux (chart pulled from this repo via a
`GitRepository`, since the published Helm repo isn't available, see #2/#7),
external PostgreSQL, Redis and RabbitMQ.

items.title: container_memory_used is always 0 on cgroup v2
items.body:
**Describe the bug**

`get_container_memory_used()` in `userspace/libsinsp/linux/resource_utilization.cpp` reads `/sys/fs/cgroup/memory/memory.usage_in_bytes`, which is a cgroup v1 path. On a cgroup v2 node that file doesn't exist, `fopen` fails, the function returns without logging anything and the value stays at 0.

With the default metrics settings a field at 0 isn't printed, so `container_memory_used` just doesn't show up in the snapshot. I only saw the 0 after setting `include_empty_values: true`.

**How to reproduce it**

Install Falco with the Helm chart on a node with cgroup v2, enable metrics with `resource_utilization_enabled: true` and `include_empty_values: true`, and look at one snapshot:

```
falco.container_memory_used_mb=0.0
falco.host_memory_used_mb=1048.6
falco.memory_pss_mb=122.9
falco.memory_rss_mb=138.9
```

From inside the Falco container (`kubectl exec -n falco <pod> -c falco`):

```
$ cat /proc/self/cgroup
0::/kubepods.slice/kubepods-burstable.slice/kubepods-burstable-pod3a13d672_47ab_45c7_b40f_ef947382d178.slice/cri-containerd-0d035b9e4e6df298b327393e58b2a31bd5274b96d8d3a44703e5251c6117a3bb.scope
$ cat /sys/fs/cgroup/memory/memory.usage_in_bytes
cat: can't open '/sys/fs/cgroup/memory/memory.usage_in_bytes': No such file or directory
$ cat /sys/fs/cgroup/memory.current
cat: can't open '/sys/fs/cgroup/memory.current': No such file or directory
$ cat /sys/fs/cgroup$(cut -d: -f3 /proc/self/cgroup)/memory.current
117444608
```

**Expected behaviour**

`container_memory_used` reports the memory of the Falco container on cgroup v2 too. Here it should be around 112 MiB.

**Environment**

- Falco version: 0.45.0 (libs 0.26.0, engine `modern_bpf`, driver 11.0.0+driver)
- System info:
```json
{
  "machine": "x86_64",
  "nodename": "falco-q722b",
  "release": "6.12.111+deb13-amd64",
  "sysname": "Linux",
  "version": "#1 SMP PREEMPT_DYNAMIC Debian 6.12.111-1 (2026-09-28)"
}
```
- Cloud provider or hardware configuration: bare metal laptop, single node k3s v1.36.5, containerd 2.3.4
- OS: Debian 13
- Kernel: 6.12.111+deb13-amd64
- Installation method: Kubernetes, `falco` Helm chart from https://falcosecurity.github.io/charts

**Additional context**

The fix isn't only swapping the file name. In a container with its own cgroup namespace the value is at `/sys/fs/cgroup/memory.current`, but the chart runs Falco privileged and containerd doesn't give a privileged container a cgroup namespace. As the output above shows, Falco sees the node's root cgroup, which has no `memory.current`, and its own value is under the path from `/proc/self/cgroup`.

I'd like to send a PR for this. Would you rather have this function resolve its own path from `/proc/self/cgroup`, or reuse the cgroup v2 support that libs already has?

Until then `FALCO_CGROUP_MEM_PATH` works as a workaround, I saw someone setting it by hand in https://github.com/falcosecurity/falco/issues/3643#issuecomment-3597482529

labels.name: kind/bug

labels.name: triage/needs-triage
labels.description: Indicates an issue needs triage by a maintainer

labels.name: area/kubernetes

items.body:
The golden worker image catalog cannot import from a Talos Image Factory that is served with a certificate from an internal CA. #3797 fixed this for the per-pool import in kubernetes-nodes by adding `talos.imageFactoryCA`, but the catalog in `packages/system/kubernetes-worker-image` did not get the same option. Its `templates/dv.yaml` renders `source.http.url` and nothing else, and the chart has no CA value.

On a cluster whose `kubernetesWorkerImage.imageFactoryURL` points at such a factory, the golden DataVolume in `cozy-public` never imports. The importer fails with `x509: certificate signed by unknown authority` and CDI restarts it with back-off. With #4802, a pool on `osImage.builtin` that clones this golden is refused at render with "keeps failing to import", so the failure is visible instead of a hang. Still, `osImage.builtin` cannot work against this factory at all. The only workaround is `osImage.factory` on every pool, which is the per-pool network import the catalog exists to avoid.

Possible fix: an optional CA value on the worker-image chart, global plus a per-image override next to `imageFactoryURL`. The chart would render it into a ConfigMap in `cozy-public` and reference it from the golden's `source.http.certConfigMap`, validated with the existing `cozy-lib.tls.validateCACert` helper. The platform's `kubernetesWorkerImage` passthrough has to forward it. With an empty default nothing is rendered and existing goldens stay as they are.

One thing to handle: a golden DataVolume spec cannot be patched. The drift check in `dv.yaml` already refuses a changed URL, storage or class on an existing golden, and adding a CA to a live golden would need the same treatment.

items.title: Kubernetes (k3s) exits when kube-router's network-policy controller hits a transient iptables error ("No chain/target/match by that name") under container churn
items.body:
### Describe the bug

OrbStack's built-in Kubernetes keeps going down during normal local development. The cause is in the embedded k3s: its NetworkPolicy controller (kube-router) calls `klog.Fatalf` when an `iptables -A` on its own `KUBE-NWPLCY-COMMON` chain fails with `No chain/target/match by that name`. That fatal takes the whole k3s process down. The API server goes with it (`127.0.0.1:26443: connection refused` from every `kubectl` call), the k8s service exits with status 2, and it is **not restarted automatically**.

The error looks like a transient race: something else changes the VM's iptables between kube-router creating the chain and appending to it. kube-router treats it as fatal instead of retrying on the next sync.

The command works most of the time, so the `icmp` / `comment` match modules are present. That points to the chain being missing at the moment of the `-A`, i.e. a race with another writer of the filter table, rather than a missing iptables extension.

Afterwards:
- `orbctl status` still says `Running`, so nothing signals that the cluster is down.
- The cluster stays down until `orbctl start k8s`.
- Pods that were running come back as stale `ContainerStatusUnknown` entries next to their replacements and have to be deleted by hand.

It is intermittent, and every occurrence lined up with heavy container or iptables churn in the VM:
1. During `docker build` of several images while the cluster is running.
2. During or right after `docker run` / `docker rm` of throwaway containers.
3. During `kubectl apply` of a large manifest set that restarts many pods at once.
4. About 20 seconds after a cold `orbctl start k8s`, while every pod is being recreated at once. In one case it fataled again right after a full `orbctl stop && orbctl start`.

With no churn, the cluster stays up for hours.

**Workaround:**
- Build images before applying manifests, and avoid `docker run`/`rm` during applies.
- After a crash: `orbctl start k8s`, then wait until `kubectl get --raw /readyz` stays `ok`. If it keeps crashing on start, `orbctl stop && orbctl start`, then `orbctl start k8s` again.
- Delete the leftover `ContainerStatusUnknown` pods.


### To Reproduce

Best effort, since it's a race:

1. Enable Kubernetes in OrbStack.
2. Apply roughly 20 Deployments plus several NetworkPolicies (default-deny ingress, per-service ingress allows, egress policies, and at least one egress `ipBlock` `0.0.0.0/0` with an `except` list of private ranges).
3. While the cluster runs, in parallel:
   - `docker build` a few images in a loop (Docker runs in the same OrbStack VM, and the images are used by the cluster as local `:dev` tags), and/or
   - `docker run -d redis:7-alpine` followed by `docker rm -f` in a loop, and
   - `kubectl rollout restart` all Deployments.
4. Within minutes, `orbctl logs k8s` shows the `network_policy_controller.go:659` fatal followed by `service k8s exited with 2`, and every `kubectl` call fails with `The connection to the server 127.0.0.1:26443 was refused`.


### Expected behavior

- A transient iptables failure in the network-policy controller should be retried on the next sync, not kill k3s.
- If k3s does exit, OrbStack should restart it, or at least show it as failed in `orbctl status`, which today still says `Running`.
- Pods that were running before the crash should not be left behind as stale `ContainerStatusUnknown` entries.

Questions:
1. Is there a supported way to pass k3s flags, e.g. `--disable-network-policy` or a different policy controller? NetworkPolicy enforcement is useful locally, but stability matters more.
2. Could the bundled kube-router be patched to retry here, or could OrbStack restart k8s automatically after this exit?


### Diagnostic report (REQUIRED)

**Environment**
- OrbStack 2.2.3 (2020300), commit c83556b0ef8f1ba9a33abbb194622b6b7a1c0307
- k3s v1.35.6+orb1 (6ffe4302); kube-router v2.6.3-k3s1; klog v2.140.0-k3s1 (from the stack trace)
- macOS 27.0.1 (26A434), Apple M3 Pro (arm64), 36 GB RAM
- OrbStack settings: `memory_mib: 16384`, `cpu: 11`, `k8s.enable: true`, `k8s.expose_services: false`
- Memory is not the problem: about 1 GB used and 14 GB available in the VM when it happened.
- Workload: about 20 Deployments plus a few StatefulSets and Jobs, and 15 enforced NetworkPolicies.

**`orbctl logs k8s`** (the same fatal each time, the last one at `F1011 15:49:11`):

```
F1011 15:37:06.513620     347 network_policy_controller.go:659] failed to run iptables command: running [/usr/sbin/iptables -t filter -A KUBE-NWPLCY-COMMON -m comment --comment allow icmp destination unreachable messages -p icmp --icmp-type destination-unreachable -j ACCEPT --wait]: exit status 1: iptables: No chain/target/match by that name.
panic: F1011 15:37:06.513620     347 network_policy_controller.go:659] failed to run iptables command: ... iptables: No chain/target/match by that name.

k8s.io/klog/v2.(*loggingT).printf(...)
	/go/pkg/mod/github.com/k3s-io/klog/v2@v2.140.0-k3s1/klog.go:761
k8s.io/klog/v2.Fatalf(...)
	/go/pkg/mod/github.com/k3s-io/klog/v2@v2.140.0-k3s1/klog.go:1688
github.com/cloudnativelabs/kube-router/v2/pkg/controllers/netpol.(*NetworkPolicyController).ensureCommonPolicyChain(0x4016a746c0)
	/go/pkg/mod/github.com/k3s-io/kube-router/v2@v2.6.3-k3s1/pkg/controllers/netpol/network_policy_controller.go:659 +0x850
github.com/cloudnativelabs/kube-router/v2/pkg/controllers/netpol.(*NetworkPolicyController).fullPolicySync(0x4016a746c0)
	/go/pkg/mod/github.com/k3s-io/kube-router/v2@v2.6.3-k3s1/pkg/controllers/netpol/network_policy_controller.go:270 +0x45c
github.com/cloudnativelabs/kube-router/v2/pkg/controllers/netpol.(*NetworkPolicyController).Run.func1(...)

created by github.com/cloudnativelabs/kube-router/v2/pkg/controllers/netpol.(*NetworkPolicyController).Run in goroutine 31031

**Client side after the crash**
```

The connection to the server 127.0.0.1:26443 was refused - did you specify the right host or port?

items.title: Agent jobs are dropped when no worker is available, so autoscaled workers can't pick up waiting SIP calls
items.body: **Describe the bug** If no agent worker is `AVAILABLE` when a job is created, the self-hosted server drops the job instead of waiting for one: - `AgentHandler.JobRequest` returns `ResourceExhausted` ([agenthandler.go#L407-L411](https://github.com/livekit/livekit/blob/c2de273198c4f8702de6d5bfbf9b83df818aa466/pkg/service/agenthandler.go#L407-L411)) - `LaunchJob` logs the error and returns ([client.go#L179-L183](https://github.com/livekit/livekit/blob/c2de273198c4f8702de6d5bfbf9b83df818aa466/pkg/agent/client.go#L179-L183)) - `launchRoomAgents` / `launchTargetAgents` run once, and nothing re-launches the dispatch when a worker registers or becomes `AVAILABLE` later ([room.go#L1785-L1832](https://github.com/livekit/livekit/blob/c2de273198c4f8702de6d5bfbf9b83df818aa466/pkg/rtc/room.go#L1785-L1832)) With autoscaled workers on Kubernetes, a new pod usually takes 1–2 minutes to register. Meanwhile, an inbound SIP caller keeps ringing (the default `ringing_timeout` is 3 min) in a room that will never get an agent, until they hang up. **Server** - Version: `v1.13.9` - Environment: self-hosted, Kubernetes, agent workers autoscaled (HPA/KEDA) - SIP: livekit/sip `v1.18.0`, inbound trunk + dispatch rule with an agent **Client** - SDK: livekit-agents (Python) - Version: `1.8.6` **To Reproduce** 1. Run livekit-server + SIP with one agent worker, and make it report FULL (busy, or a low `load_threshold`). Not running any worker also works. 2. Place an inbound call, or create a room with an agent dispatch. 3. The server logs `no worker available to handle job` and `failed to send job request`. 4. Start a second worker. It registers but never receives the job, and the caller keeps ringing. **Expected behavior** The server should hold the job for a bounded time (for example, up to the dispatch or ringing deadline) and assign it as soon as a worker registers or becomes `AVAILABLE`. LiveKit Cloud already seems to do this ([forum thread](https://community.livekit.io/t/inbound-sip-call-agent-job-dispatched-8s-after-the-invite-reached-livekit-cloud-caller-had-already-hung-up/1393)). A metric for dropped or pending dispatches would also give autoscalers a signal to act on before calls are lost. I'm happy to open a PR if this direction works for you. **Additional context** Probably the same root cause: #3857, #4060, #4259, livekit/agents#3202, livekit/agents#7102 (in #7102, a worker was wrongly marked FULL for 2.5 s and that cost a call).

items.title: Migrate to the Freelens v2 extension API
items.body:
## Goal

Port this extension from the Freelens v1 extension API to the **v2 extension API**, so that it loads and works on Freelens 2.x, and align its build stack with the current Freelens stack.

The work is done mostly by the Claude agent in CI (`.github/workflows/claude.yaml`), one or more steps per @<!-- -->claude comment from a maintainer, with maintainers reviewing each step and answering with another @<!-- -->claude comment when it needs corrections. This issue is the plan; the PR is the working record.

> **Template note.** This issue is a copy of the template freelensapp/freelens-example-extension#326, made with the [`port-freelens-extension-to-v2`](https://github.com/freelensapp/freelens-example-extension/blob/main/skills/port-freelens-extension-to-v2/SKILL.md) skill. Sections marked **(generic)** are copied as they are, with their findings. Sections marked **(project-specific)** are rewritten for this repository: the inventory, the functional checks and the project's decisions.
>
> **No trigger in the body.** The CI agent also starts when an issue whose body contains the literal mention is opened. Every mention of it here is split with an HTML comment (`@<!-- -->claude` in the source), so opening a copy of this issue does not start a run; keep it that way when editing or copying.
>
> **Feature issues.** This issue covers the extension itself: manifest, build, TypeScript layout, tests, CI, docs and the components shared across features. Adapting the extension's own features goes into a separate issue per feature, worked on in the same PR. Here: #71 (chat page and "Ask Claude" menu items, steps `C0`...), #72 (preferences page, steps `P0`...) and #73 (main process: bridge, Claude session and Kubernetes tools, steps `B0`...).
>
> **Living document.** The v2 specification was written before any real extension was ported, so this description is expected to change as the migration finds what the specification did not foresee. Each such finding is recorded under "Findings" and folded into the section it affects, so that later copies of the template inherit it.

## Source of truth (generic)

Read these before writing any code. They are pinned to freelensapp/freelens@f568c9c51eab1fd4860f282826b13fc357d92949, the commit the `@freelensapp/extensions` nightly below was built from. The docs, the fixture extension, the stack versions and the metafiles are all read at this one commit; when the nightly is bumped, the pin moves with it. Once Freelens 2.0.0 is released, the pin becomes the `v2.0.0` tag and the `@freelensapp/extensions` dependency a semver range.

- [`docs/extensions/migrating-from-v1.md`](https://github.com/freelensapp/freelens/blob/f568c9c51eab1fd4860f282826b13fc357d92949/docs/extensions/migrating-from-v1.md) - the porting guide, including the final checklist
- [`docs/extensions/api.md`](https://github.com/freelensapp/freelens/blob/f568c9c51eab1fd4860f282826b13fc357d92949/docs/extensions/api.md) - the normative contracts C1-C14
- [`docs/extensions/binaries.md`](https://github.com/freelensapp/freelens/blob/f568c9c51eab1fd4860f282826b13fc357d92949/docs/extensions/binaries.md) - shipped executables and process invocation
- [`packages/fixture-extension/`](https://github.com/freelensapp/freelens/tree/f568c9c51eab1fd4860f282826b13fc357d92949/packages/fixture-extension) - the in-repo v2 extension: `vite.config.mjs`, `tsconfig.base.json`, per-environment `tsconfig.json`, `environment-tests/`
- [`scripts/vite-plugin-standard-decorators.mjs`](https://github.com/freelensapp/freelens/blob/f568c9c51eab1fd4860f282826b13fc357d92949/scripts/vite-plugin-standard-decorators.mjs) - MIT, may be copied

The type surface to compile against is `@freelensapp/extensions@2.0.0-0-nightly-2026-10-11`, published under the `nightly` dist-tag. If the docs and the published `extension-api.d.ts` disagree, the `.d.ts` wins and the discrepancy is reported in the PR.

This repository, the template, is read at its current `main`, not at the pin. Its build, tooling, CI and Renovate setup are the patterns this plan points to, and they keep changing with the findings of later ports, so take its files as they are on `main` when the step runs. The library and tool versions still follow "Stack alignment": where a file on `main` carries a version ahead of the pin, keep the file from `main`, set that version to the pinned one and say so in the PR. Do not take the files from an older commit of this repository to match the pin: that also drops the changes that do not depend on it, see "Findings".

## Stack alignment with Freelens (generic)

The build stack is aligned with the current Freelens stack at the pinned commit, not merely made to work with v2. Where Freelens has an equivalent, copy its choice rather than inventing one, and note every deliberate deviation in the PR.

| What | Reference in freelensapp/freelens | Applies to the extension as |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Library versions | `pnpm-workspace.yaml` `catalog:` | same exact versions: `react`/`react-dom`/`@types/react`/`@types/react-dom` 19.3.0, `mobx` 7.0.6, `mobx-react` 10.0.2, `typescript` 7.0.2, `vite` 8.3.4, `vitest` 5.0.3, `esbuild` 0.28.2, `@vitejs/plugin-react` 6.1.2, `@testing-library/react` 16.3.3, `jsdom` 30.1.1, `sass-embedded` 1.105.1 (replaces `sass`), `@types/node` 24.19.1, `electron` 43.7.9; any other library the extension uses that is in the catalog takes the catalog version |
| Tool versions in scripts | root `package.json` | `@biomejs/biome@2.5.15`, `knip@6.39.0`, `@trunkio/launcher@1.3.4` |
| Package manager | root `package.json` `packageManager`, `pnpm-workspace.yaml` | `pnpm@12.11.1`, with the pnpm 12 settings that apply to a single package (for example `allowBuilds` in place of `onlyBuiltDependencies`), plus `strictPeerDependencies: true`, as the migration guide recommends for extensions (Freelens itself does not set it): it makes the peer ranges of `@freelensapp/extensions` fail the install when a shared library of the extension drifts from them |
| Vite config | `packages/fixture-extension/vite.config.mjs` | the base for `vite.config.mjs`: plain Vite, ESM, one run per entry (`vite build` and `vite build --mode main`), host modules resolved by an `enforce: "pre"` plugin; the main run sets `build.rolldownOptions.platform: "node"`, so that a bundled CommonJS package that `require()`s a Node builtin gets a `require` made with `createRequire(import.meta.url)` instead of a shim that throws, see "Findings" |
| Decorators | `scripts/vite-plugin-standard-decorators.mjs` | copied into `build/`, used by the Vite and Vitest configs |
| CSS module declarations | none: Freelens commits no CSS module declarations | [`build/vite-plugin-css-module-declarations.mjs`](https://github.com/freelensapp/freelens-example-extension/blob/main/build/vite-plugin-css-module-declarations.mjs) of freelensapp/freelens-example-extension, copied unchanged into `build/` and registered for the renderer run; it writes the committed `*.module.d.scss.ts` files in place of `vite-plugin-sass-dts`, which is removed, see "Findings" |

## Findings (generic)

Things the migration needed that the v2 specification and this plan did not cover. One entry per finding: what was found, the evidence (link to the PR comment), the sections of this issue it changed, and whether it needs a change upstream (then it also gets an entry under "Upstream work item").

- **The pin must be the commit the nightly was built from.** The stack versions listed under "Stack alignment" were taken from Freelens `main`, while the references were pinned to an older commit (6452e83) with different versions; the nightly package was built from `main`. Evidence: https://github.com/freelensapp/freelens-example-extension/pull/328#issuecomment-6037544090. Changed: "Source of truth" now pins everything to the nightly's commit (2f1410f), which leaves the docs, the fixture extension and the decorators plugin as they were at 6452e83. Upstream: nothing to report.
- **`@observable` without `accessor` passes the type check.** After `makeObservable(this)` is removed, a field decorator on a plain field type-checks and builds; mobx's development build throws `Please use @observable accessor …` when the class is defined, and the production build silently leaves the field unobservable. Freelens itself has no check for it either (neither the decorators plugin nor `type:check`). Evidence: https://github.com/freelensapp/freelens-example-extension/pull/328#issuecomment-6037544368. Changed: nothing here; this extension follows Freelens, so the check belongs upstream first. Upstream: yes; the guide now says it (freelensapp/freelens#2654), the build-time check is deferred.
- **The migration guide still says the host `require()`s the entry.** "Styling and CSS" in `migrating-from-v1.md` says the host loads an extension by `require()`-ing its JS entry, which contradicts C4 and the guide's own "the renderer entry is ESM, loaded by URL". Evidence: https://github.com/freelensapp/freelens-example-extension/pull/328#issuecomment-6037498731 ("Doc inconsistency"). Changed: nothing here. Upstream: yes, fixed in freelensapp/freelens#2654.
- **An extension cannot take the shared library versions from `@freelensapp/extensions`.** Under pnpm's isolated layout the `@types/react` and `@types/react-dom` in the package's `dependencies` are invisible to the extension's own code (`TS7016` in every `.tsx` without its own copy), and a different pin by the extension installs a second copy silently. The optional peers do not supply versions; they only check the ones the extension declares, as one warning line unless `strictPeerDependencies` is set. Required peers would check nothing more and add downloads (`monaco-editor`, the newest Electron major). Evidence: https://github.com/freelensapp/freelens-example-extension/pull/328#issuecomment-6039102566 (experiment 4). Changed: "Package manager" adds `strictPeerDependencies: true`, so the Freelens peer ranges fail the install instead of warning. Upstream: yes; `@types/react`, `@types/react-dom` and `react-dom` are optional peers since freelensapp/freelens#2654, so `strictPeerDependencies` now checks them too.
- **Vite hides a Node import in the renderer and leaves `process.env.NODE_ENV` in place.** With the builtins no longer external, Vite replaces a renderer import of `node:fs` (in the extension or in a bundled library) with an empty `__vite-browser-external` module and only warns, so the build succeeds and the import is `undefined` at runtime; library mode also leaves `process.env.NODE_ENV` for a consumer's bundler, while the renderer has no guaranteed `process`. Evidence: https://github.com/freelensapp/freelens-example-extension/pull/328#issuecomment-6040112432. Changed: handled in the build (a plugin that fails the renderer build on a Node or Electron import, and a renderer `define`), documented in `AGENTS.md` as part of the build pattern. Upstream: no; it is bundler behaviour, outside the contract.
- **Environment tests compiled on their own cannot catch a leak from a dependency.** The fixture's environment configs use `include: []`, and the guide describes compiling "a file of lines that must fail with each config". A third-party declaration with `/// <reference types="node" />` or `/// <reference lib="dom" />` enters a program only when a source file imports it, so a probe compiled alone never reaches it, and the source program has no line that would fail. Evidence: https://github.com/freelensapp/freelens-example-extension/pull/328#issuecomment-6041878466 (a fake package with `/// <reference types="node" />` imported by the renderer: the fixture-style config passes, the same probe compiled with the sources fails with 4 unused directives; reproduced locally). Changed: "Environment tests" compiles the probes together with the sources. Upstream: yes, folded into the "Source layout" entry; fixed in the guide and the fixture by freelensapp/freelens#2654.
- **The host logs a 404 console error for each stylesheet candidate an extension does not ship.** The extension loader requests `<entry>.css` and then `style.css` without stopping at the first one it links, and each missing one leaves `Failed to load resource: … 404` in the renderer console, so the integration test, which fails on any console error, fails for an extension that ships exactly `renderer.css` as C10 asks. Evidence: https://github.com/freelensapp/freelens-example-extension/actions/runs/37666083866. Changed: nothing here. Upstream: yes, filed separately as freelensapp/freelens#2651 because it blocked the integration tests; fixed on Freelens `main` by freelensapp/freelens#2652 (764bc1995), and the integration tests pass against it: https://github.com/freelensapp/freelens-example-extension/actions/runs/37666083866 (attempt 2).
- **knip's Vite plugin drops the renderer from the `--production` pass.** With `vite.config.mjs` in library mode, the plugin registers `build.lib.entry` as a development entry, which replaces the `src/renderer/index.tsx!` production entry, so `knip --production --strict` skips the renderer. Evidence: https://github.com/freelensapp/freelens-example-extension/pull/328#issuecomment-6043860488. Changed: "Knip" here runs with the Vite plugin off and `vite.config.mjs` listed as an entry. Upstream: yes, the fixture's knip workspace had the same shape; fixed in freelensapp/freelens#2654.
- **Renovate proposes versions ahead of Freelens.** Renovate looks the shared libraries and tools up in their registries, so it raises PRs for versions Freelens has not adopted yet (jsdom 30.1.2, vite 8.3.3, knip 6.40.0, electron 43.7.8, Biome 2.5.15, while Freelens is on 30.1.1, 8.3.2, 6.39.0, 43.7.7 and 2.5.4), and the versions that must match the host were kept in line by hand with `ignoreDeps` and major/minor limits. Evidence: the open Renovate PRs after freelensapp/freelens-example-extension#328 was merged. Changed: "Renovate" in "Stack alignment"; the rules read the versions from Freelens on `main` through custom datasources (YAML, JSON and TOML) with `overrideDatasource`, with `rangeStrategy: "replace"` (the datasource returns one release, and `bump` skips a dependency without a lock file whose current version is not among them), `minimumReleaseAge: "0 days"` (no release dates) and, for mise tools from GitHub, `extractVersion: "^v?(?<version>.+)$"`; checked with `renovate --platform=local --dry-run=lookup` against lowered versions. Commit eafa925. Upstream: no.
- **A cluster page gets only `params`, and the types do not say so.** The host renders a `clusterPages` component as `<ObserverPage params={normalizedParams} />` (`packages/core/src/renderer/routes/extension-route-registrator.injectable.tsx`), while `PageComponents.Page` in the v2 declaration is `React.ComponentType<any>`. A page whose props require more, such as the extension instance, compiles and gets `undefined` at runtime; here the `Example` page never received `extension`, which only shows once its error page tries to log. Evidence: https://github.com/freelensapp/freelens-example-extension/issues/327#issuecomment-6060625899 and PR freelensapp/freelens-example-extension#336. Changed: nothing generic here; a page that needs the extension gets it from the registration (`Page: () => <Page extension={this} />`), see freelensapp/freelens-example-extension#327. Upstream: yes, filed as freelensapp/freelens#2655; fixed by freelensapp/freelens#2656 in the 2026-10-09 nightly, where `Page` is typed with `PageComponentProps` and the type check rejects a page that requires another prop.

Changed: nothing here. Changed: the "CSS module declarations" row of "Stack alignment" and step 2, in freelensapp/freelens-example-extension#344 (freelensapp/freelens-example-extension#343). Changed: "Validation by maintainers" links the new "Checking the Extension in Freelens Dev" section of `AGENTS.md`, added in freelensapp/freelens-example-extension#347. Upstream: no; Freelens's `DEVELOPMENT.md` already covers attaching the agent.

## Rules for the CI agent (generic)

- Each run is started by a maintainer's @<!-- -->claude comment: on this issue until the PR exists, on the PR afterwards. Do what that comment asks and nothing beyond it.
- The first run creates the branch `claude/issue-<this issue number>-migrate-freelens-api-v2` and opens one PR as a draft (`gh pr create --draft`). GitHub needs a commit to open a PR and step 0 changes no code, so that run starts the branch with an empty commit (`git commit --allow-empty`); the repository squash-merges, so it leaves no trace on `main`. The PR has `Closes #<this issue>` and `Closes #<feature issue>` for every feature issue in its description; the PR description mirrors the checklists of this issue and, in a separate section per feature issue headed as project-specific, the checklist of that issue, all kept in sync.
- Steps of this issue are numbered (`0`-`7`), steps of a feature issue carry its own prefix (`C0`, `C1`, ... for #71, `P0`, ... for #72, `B0`, ... for #73). Name the step in every commit body and report comment, so it is always clear which issue a change belongs to. A finding about the v2 API or the migration in general goes here; a finding about one feature goes to its issue.
- Do not change anything under `.github/`. When a step needs a workflow change, write the complete new or changed workflow files under `github-workflow-fix/` in the repository root, with the same file names as in `.github/workflows/`, commit them with the step, list them in the report and note them in the PR description as proposed workflow changes, as "Modifying GitHub Actions Workflows" in the Freelens `AGENTS.md` describes. Maintainers move them into `.github/workflows/` in a separate commit and remove `github-workflow-fix/`. Pull before continuing, as the branch may have gained such commits.
- One commit per step; plain commit subjects, no Conventional Commits prefix; no emoji. A correction requested in a review comment is a new commit, not a rewrite of the step's commit.
- A run does the steps its comment asks for, one or more, in order. After each step, before the next one starts: run its validation, commit, push to the PR branch, update the checklists in the PR description and post the step's report. A run cut off by the job timeout or the turn limit then loses at most the step in progress.
- Stop early, after pushing and reporting the step, when it needs a workflow change under `github-workflow-fix/` that the next steps depend on, when a validation fails for a reason outside the step, or when a `Finding:` changes the plan. Say why the run stopped and which step comes next.
- What usually ends a long run is the turn limit of `claude.yaml` (`--max-turns 400`), not its 2 hour timeout. A trigger comment asks for a set of steps that fits in it. Before the turns or the time run short, stop at a step boundary and say which step comes next.
- The system prompt of the CI agent is `AGENTS.md` from `main`, which describes the v1 setup until this PR is merged. Where it disagrees with this issue on anything the migration changes (build, dependencies, host globals, layout), this issue wins; the PR branch's own `AGENTS.md` is the one being updated.
- The workflow checks out freelensapp/freelens `main` at `tmp/freelens`. The references in "Source of truth" are pinned to a commit; the checkout is shallow, so fetch that commit first (`git -C tmp/freelens fetch --depth 1 origin <sha>`) and read them there (`git -C tmp/freelens show <sha>:<path>`), and report as a finding anything relevant that `main` has changed since. `.gitignore` ignores `/tmp/` from step 1 on; without it, Biome finds the checkout's own root `biome.jsonc` and `pnpm biome:check` fails.
- When the work needs something the specification or this plan does not cover, or contradicts it, report it in the PR as a separate comment headed `Finding:`, with the evidence (error output, the `.d.ts` excerpt, the doc section) and the change to this issue you propose. Do not edit this issue yourself; maintainers fold findings in. If the finding needs a change in freelensapp/freelens, say so and propose the entry for "Upstream work item"; do not open issues or pull requests there.
- Do not work around a missing API symbol with `as any`, `globalThis.require` or reaching into host internals. Report it instead; per the migration guide a missing re-export is an upstream bug.
- Follow the repository's `AGENTS.md`.

items.body:
## Summary

With the official SkillHub 0.2.22 OCI Helm chart and web image, requests routed through the Web service return HTTP 502 on Kubernetes. The web Deployment still sets `SKILLHUB_API_UPSTREAM=http://skillhub-server:8080`, but Nginx now resolves the variable-based upstream through its runtime `resolver`, which does not expand the Kubernetes pod DNS search suffixes.

This is a Kubernetes compatibility regression following the dynamic-resolution change related to #898, not a request to revert that fix.

## Environment

- Official chart: `oci://ghcr.io/iflytek/charts/skillhub`, version `0.2.22`
- Chart OCI digest: `sha256:bb92f91f50ef6c96fba8d83841ba3d9e505a5be5f4eca7bcfb632ea6c9d1c929`
- SkillHub Web and Server images: `v0.2.22`
- Kubernetes 1.32, Helm 3.18.0
- Release/namespace: `skillhub`; cluster DNS domain: `cluster.local`
- Gateway forwards requests to `skillhub-web:80` (the Chart-generated Ingress is disabled).

## Steps to reproduce

1. Deploy the official 0.2.22 OCI chart with valid credentials and dependencies.
2. Access `/api/web/skills`, `/api/web/labels`, or `/api/v1/auth/me` through the Web service. A port-forward to the Web service is also suitable to isolate this route.
3. Inspect the generated Web environment and Nginx config:

   ```nginx
   set $skillhub_api_upstream "http://skillhub-server:8080";
   location /api/ {
       proxy_pass $skillhub_api_upstream;
   }
   ```

4. Compare an explicit DNS A query for `skillhub-server` with `skillhub-server.skillhub.svc.cluster.local` against the cluster DNS server.

## Actual result and evidence

- Web API requests return HTTP 502, while the static homepage and `/nginx-health` return 200. Consequently, Web pods can remain Ready despite the broken backend proxy.
- Nginx logs report:

  ```text
  skillhub-server could not be resolved (3: Host not found)
  ```

- Direct A lookup of the short name returns NXDOMAIN; the fully qualified service name resolves to the Server Service IP.
- From both Web pods, direct requests to `http://skillhub-server.skillhub.svc.cluster.local:8080/api/web/skills` return 200; unauthenticated `/api/v1/auth/me` returns the expected 401.
- Changing the generated upstream to the service FQDN restored proxied APIs to 200 and the OAuth authorization endpoint to its expected 302 redirect in this deployment.

## Expected result

The official Helm chart should generate a DNS name that works with Nginx runtime resolution, including the release namespace and configurable cluster DNS domain, while keeping the backend port and name overrides intact. Dynamic re-resolution should remain enabled.

## Why `web.extraEnv` is not a reliable workaround

The chart appends `web.extraEnv` after its built-in environment entries, without deduplication. Adding another `SKILLHUB_API_UPSTREAM` renders two entries with the same name. In an actual Helm upgrade from a single FQDN entry to this duplicate-entry manifest, the Helm release manifest retained both entries, but the live Deployment and new pods retained only the short-name value; 502 responses returned.

This observation concerns the Helm merge/update path, not kubelet precedence for an unchanged duplicate list. Rendering success and an API-server dry-run did not establish upgrade safety.

## Proposed fix

- Generate a namespace-qualified, full Server service DNS name in the Helm Web upstream.
- Support non-default Kubernetes cluster DNS domains without duplicate environment overrides.
- Add chart regression coverage for default/custom namespaces, service name overrides, custom ports and cluster domains.
- Preserve the dynamic Nginx resolver behavior from #898.

No application API response-shape change is required.

items.title: run a command with forwards up and stop them when it exits

labels.name: kind:feature
labels.description: New behavior nobody has built yet

items.body:
`kftui` could start the forwards, run a command like `npm test` or `psql`, and stop the forwards when the command exits. Today a script starts `kftui --auto-start --non-interactive` in the background, waits for the port, runs the command and then kills `kftui`.

## Why

- https://github.com/hcavarsan/kftray/issues/395: a user asked to start a forward from the command line and then run a CLI command against it. The flags added in v0.20.2 cover the first step only.
- https://github.com/hashicorp/terraform-provider-kubernetes/issues/812: 141 reactions. The author runs `kubectl port-forward` in a background loop while Terraform runs.
- https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/97549: asks for `kubectl port-forward ... -- psql ...`. The workaround in the thread leaves the forward running when the command fails under `set -e` or the script gets interrupted.

## How it works

Everything after `--` is the command: `kftui --configs-path team.json --auto-start -- npm test`. kftui starts the forwards and runs the command in the same terminal with no TUI. When the command exits, kftui stops the forwards and exits with the command's exit code. If no forward starts, the command does not run. The desktop app and MCP stay out.

items.body:
_(re-filed 2026-10-11; replaces a deleted issue, formerly number 5757; originally by `systemorph-com[bot]` on 2026-09-26)_

**What is failing.** FleetWatch's `StalePortal` roll alarm fired for two fleet instances: `build` is still running `3.0.0-ci.8411` while `3.0.0-ci.9406` is the newest promoted build (a compatible newer build was first promoted 7 d 11 h ago), and `client-b` is on `3.0.0-ci.9077` (4 d 2 h behind). In both cases the blocking reason recorded is the same: **no self-update Roll was opened by the instance's self-updater for any build newer than the one it runs** — the updater has not announced one. On `build` the alarm additionally carries `pending_module_activation: Degraded` — 35 modules (the whole `MeshWeaver.AI.*` family, `MeshWeaver.Azure.Blob`, …) are landed but not loaded in the running process, plus 1 module REFUSED, so the instance is also feature-degraded until a restart.

The alarm itself is working as designed ([FleetWatch](/Hosting/FleetWatch) — "roll, restart, observe"); the defect is that the self-update loop that should have rolled these portals never announced a Roll.

**Probable cause.** The self-updater on the affected instances has stopped opening Roll announcements for newer compatible builds. Confidence: medium — the alarm text names the ground ("its self-updater has not announced one"), but the evidence does not distinguish between a stuck self-updater process, an `Admin/UpdatePolicy` blocked by merge-guard/update-queue failures (the log history around `Admin/UpdatePolicy` shows repeated `UpdateQueue FAILED` / `MergeGuard refused` / `could not record the check verdict` entries on the `memex-cloud` pod in the days before), or a deliberately conservative policy. A secondary symptom on `build` — 35 landed-but-unloaded modules needing a restart — is consistent with a long-lived process that has not restarted in a week, which a working roll cadence (bound: two CD cycles = 6 h) would have forced.

**Impact.** Both portals are still serving (no outage), but `build` has been running a 7-day-old build and is feature-degraded (AI modules landed but not active). 2 occurrences on one observing pod, first seen 2026-09-26T12:22Z; the underlying staleness itself goes back to 2026-09-19 (build) and 2026-09-22 (client-b). The CD roll guarantee — a portal no more than ~6 h behind the newest promoted build — is broken for two of the fleet's instances.

**Where to look.** Start with the self-updater on the affected instances: read each instance's `Admin/UpdatePolicy` and its self-update log as the alarm instructs, and check the `UpdateQueue`/`MergeGuard`/`SelfUpdate` log categories (repeated `FAILED path=Admin/UpdatePolicy` lines and stale/reordered cross-hub write refusals appear in `Ops/Logs` in the preceding days — see the `memex-cloud` pod entries). Also check whether the refused module on `build` blocks activation. Related prior work: MeshWeaver#4471 (self-update configuration lambda never ran), #5011, #5384.

items.title: Upgrading from 2026.1.0/2026.1.1 to 2026.1.2 fails: StatefulSet selector is immutable
items.body:
Upgrading a release installed with chart **2026.1.1** (and, from the template history, 2026.1.0) to **2026.1.2** fails with the default `oldNamingStyle: true`:

```
Error: UPGRADE FAILED: ... StatefulSet.apps "yb-master" is invalid: spec.selector:
Invalid value: {"matchLabels":{"app":"yb-master"}}: field is immutable
(same for yb-tserver)
```

**Reproduce** (Helm v4.2.1, kind / Kubernetes 1.37; a one-master, one-tserver universe was enough):

```sh
helm repo add yugabytedb https://charts.yugabyte.com
helm install yb yugabytedb/yugabyte --version 2026.1.1 -n yb --create-namespace --wait
helm upgrade yb yugabytedb/yugabyte --version 2026.1.2 -n yb --wait
```

**Cause.** 9f20ba628 ([PLAT-22174]) moves `release:` inside the `else` branch of `yugabyte.appselector`, so with `oldNamingStyle: true` the StatefulSet selector goes from `{app, release}` (2026.1.0 and 2026.1.1) back to `{app}` (2024.2, 2025.2 and 2026.1.2). That fixes upgrades from the 2025.2 line, which is what the commit set out to do, but StatefulSet selectors can't change. So every universe installed with 2026.1.0 or 2026.1.1 now hits the same error in the other direction.

**Workaround.** Deleting the StatefulSets without their pods (`kubectl delete sts yb-master yb-tserver --cascade=orphan`) lets the upgrade go through: Helm recreates them with the new selector and they adopt the existing pods and volumes. I could only verify that far. On kind, the 2026.1.2 pods then failed to write to the data directory, which I believe comes from kind's local-path storage ignoring `fsGroup` rather than from the chart.

**Possible fix.** Keep whatever selector the existing StatefulSet has, so both upgrade paths work, for example:

```yaml
{{- $sts := lookup "apps/v1" "StatefulSet" .Release.Namespace $name }}
{{- if $sts }}{{ toYaml $sts.spec.selector.matchLabels }}{{ else }}...current logic...{{ end }}
```

Or document the orphan-delete step for 2026.1.0/2026.1.1 users in the 2026.1.2 release notes. Happy to open a PR for either.

(Found with [Helmbulance](https://github.com/egezamb/helmbulance), a tool I'm building that tests chart upgrades on a throwaway cluster.)

items.title: [4.22.1] Container fails to start: application compiled for Java 25 but image uses Java 21
items.body:
### Describe the bug

Hello,

Apache Camel Karavan 4.22.1 fails to start on Kubernetes with an `UnsupportedClassVersionError`.

**Environment**
- Karavan: 4.22.1
- Deployment: Kubernetes, managed through Rancher
- Image: `ghcr.io/apache/camel-karavan:4.22.1`, pulled through a Harbor proxy cache

**Steps to reproduce**
1. Deploy the Karavan 4.22.1 image with the required configuration.
2. Start the container.
3. Check the application logs.

**Actual behavior**

The application fails during startup:

```text
java.lang.UnsupportedClassVersionError:
org/apache/camel/karavan/service/NotificationService
has been compiled by a more recent version of the Java Runtime
(class file version 69.0), this version of the Java Runtime
only recognizes class file versions up to 65.0
```

**Expected behavior**

The published container image should include a Java runtime compatible with the packaged application.

**Identified mismatch**

In the `4.22.1` source tag:

`karavan-app/pom.xml`:
```xml
<maven.compiler.source>25</maven.compiler.source>
<maven.compiler.release>25</maven.compiler.release>
```

`karavan-app/src/main/docker/Dockerfile`:
```dockerfile
FROM eclipse-temurin:21-jdk
```

Class file version **69** corresponds to Java **25**, while version **65** corresponds to Java **21**.

**Tested workaround**

I used an init container to copy `/opt/app/karavan.jar` from the Karavan image into a shared volume, then executed the same JAR in a container based on `eclipse-temurin:25-jdk`.

The application started successfully with this workaround.

**Suggested fix**

Align the container runtime with the application's compilation target, for example by updating the Dockerfile base image to:

```dockerfile
FROM eclipse-temurin:25-jdk
```

Please also consider adding a startup smoke test for the built image to detect this mismatch before publication.

Thank you.

Web Application

Kubernetes

4.22.1

items.title: Lockfile not removed upon stop of container
items.body:
### Bug description

After `docker stop`, `/data/Config/options.json.lock` remains. This especially causes container restarts for updates to fail, because for some reason beyond me FoundryVTT uses a lock dir lib that considers the lock held if it's less than 10s old, instead of using flock.

The same issue happens with FoundryVTT in Kubernetes.

**Cause:** On SIGTERM, `wait "$child_pid"` in `entrypoint.sh` returns 143. errexit then ends the entrypoint, which is PID 1, and the kernel kills node with SIGKILL before FoundryVTT has a chance to remove its lockfile.

**Workaround:** I build a custom container anyway to embed FoundryVTT. There, I now also change the entrypoint's launcher call to `exec ./launcher.sh "$@"`, so that no more waiting happens. Launcher in return execs into node, so FoundryVTT can handle docker's SIGTERM upon container stop directly.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Start the container with a volume for `/data`
2. `docker stop` it
3. Lock is left in `/data/Config`
4. Next start within 10s fails / container remains stopped, so automatic updates of mine fail

### Expected behavior

Upon docker stop, FoundryVTT should terminate gracefully and remove its lockfile.

### Container metadata

```shell
N/A, but happens with any (v13, v14) and the latest version at time of writing.
```

### Relevant log output

```console
No log output follows upon termination due to the container being killed.
```

items.title: [Regression][Linux] Native HttpCloak/Koffi calls followed by GC hang Bun 1.4.3; 1.4.2 completes
items.body:
### What version of Bun is running?

1.4.3+c6da4a4d3

### What platform is your computer?

Linux 6.8.0-146-generic x86_64 unknown

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

Observed on Linux x86_64 inside a container, with Bun `1.4.3+c6da4a4d3` and `httpcloak@1.7.2`.

1. Create a directory, save the attached script as repro.ts, and install its dependency:
```sh
bun init -y
bun add --exact httpcloak@1.7.2
```

2. Run the reproduction with an external watchdog:
```sh
timeout --kill-after=5s 30s bun repro.ts
echo "exit code: $?"
```
3. Repeat using Bun 1.4.2 on the same host, in the same container, with the same script and dependencies.

The script starts a loopback-only HTTP server, creates a native HttpCloak session, and performs six GET/POST pairs. Concurrently, it allocates memory and calls Bun.gc(true) every 100 ms. It prints a heartbeat every five seconds and checks HTTP responsiveness before and after a 20-second observation period.

No external service, authentication credentials, database, or application code is required.

### What is the expected behavior?

The script continues printing heartbeats, reports:

```json
{"healthStatuses":[200,200]}
```

and exits with code 0.

### What do you see instead?

Heartbeat output stops and the script does not complete. The external watchdog terminates it with exit code 124.

Observed output:

```text
{"collections":31}
{"collections":79}
```

### Additional information

### Comparison with Bun 1.4.2

The same reproduction completed successfully in the same production container:

```text
{"collections":44}
{"collections":91}
{"collections":138}
{"collections":187}
{"healthStatuses":[200,200]}
```

Exit code: 0.

### Additional context

The production application also stopped responding to HTTP health probes shortly after successful native HTTP operations, causing Kubernetes to restart the containers.

This appears platform-dependent: local WSL runs did not reproduce the hang. The exact internal mechanism is unknown; we have not captured a native stack trace. Pinning the application runtime to Bun 1.4.2 is our current workaround.

items.title: [4.22.1] Missing action buttons on individual steps in the web Designer
items.body:
Hello,

In Apache Camel Karavan **4.22.1**, the action buttons (delete, copy, and disable) are missing from individual steps on the Designer canvas. For example, a Logger step cannot be deleted through the canvas.

**Environment**
- Karavan 4.22.1 — Web Application
- Kubernetes, managed through Rancher
- Karavan environment: `dev`
- Browser: Google Chrome on macOS

**Steps to reproduce**
1. Create a project and a route with a Timer and a Logger.
2. Select or hover over the Logger.
3. Observe that no action buttons appear.

**Expected behavior**

The applicable action buttons should appear when hovering over the step.

**Actual behavior**

The buttons are absent, including in private browsing mode.

**Identified cause**

In `karavan-app/src/main/webui/src/ui/designer/route/element/DslElementHeader.tsx`, the buttons are rendered with:

```tsx
{isRoute && isDev && getHeaderButtons()}
```

The `isRoute` condition excludes individual steps such as `LogDefinition`.

**Tested workaround**

Removing the `isRoute` condition:

```tsx
{isDev && getHeaderButtons()}
```

I tested the equivalent change in the compiled JavaScript inside the application JAR. After restarting the application and disabling the browser cache, the buttons appeared and the reported issue was resolved.

This was a targeted UI test, not a full regression test.

Could you confirm whether this restriction is intentional and consider including a fix in a future release?

Thank you.

items.body:
Part of #790 (area 2: a fresh install as a stranger). Compose part only; the Helm install is a later batch.

## What was run

- **Release:** v0.7.1, from the release's `compose.yaml` and `.env.example`, following only `docs/DEPLOYING.md`.
- **Two changes to the compose file**, so it could not touch another stack on the same host: the project name (`javv-hunt`) and the host port (8090).
- **Scanners:** a new k3d cluster (k3s v1.35.5) with the `javv-scanner` 0.7.1 chart from the release. `helm test` passed for both tokens, and one Trivy and one Grype cycle ran by hand, as the chart's notes say.
- **Verify the images and charts:** cosign verify and the SBOM attestation pass for both app images; all three charts verify.
- **Screens:** every route, empty and then with data. A person walked them too. The route smoke ran read-only, and the triage loop was done by hand (acknowledge, reload, revert).
- **No internet:** the same release on an internal Docker network, and a browser that cannot reach the font hosts.

**One step left the documented path:** the first two tokens were minted with `POST /api/v1/admin/tokens`, because of finding 1.

## Findings

| # | Severity | Finding |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | high | A fresh install cannot mint its first token from the UI |
| 2 | high | Images of digest-pinned pods are never scanned |
| 3 | medium | Three settings pages never load before the first cluster |
| 4 | medium | A skipped image disappears from the UI without a sign |
| 5 | medium | A refused findings search reads as "no findings" |
| 6 | medium | Behind a firewall that drops packets, every page load is blank for about 22 s |
| 7 | low | Two installs on one host share one compose project |
| 8 | low | The empty-state action is a button inside a link |
| 9 | design | The primary button gives no feedback on a press (needs a ruling) |

### 1. A fresh install cannot mint its first token from the UI (high)

- **What happens:** the mint dialog's Cluster field is a `<select>` of the clusters JAVV knows (`frontend/src/views/settings/TokensView.vue:282`). A fresh install knows none, so the list is empty and **Mint token** stays disabled. Checked live: 0 options, button disabled.
- **What the docs say:** `docs/DEPLOYING.md` step 2 of "Connect the scanners" says to enter the cluster ID.
- **Why it matters:** the "Create a scanner token" button on every empty screen leads to this dialog. The field has been a select since #407, and the test rigs mint through the API, so no test reaches this state.
- **Workarounds that exist today:** `POST /api/v1/admin/tokens` accepts any well-formed cluster ID (201). `python -m backend.core.tokens` also works, but the install docs do not name it.
- **Note:** minting the first token registers the cluster. It appears at once, named by its ID.

### 2. Images of digest-pinned pods are never scanned (high)

- **Cause:** discovery takes the image reference from `container_statuses[].image` (`scanner/src/scanner/discovery.py:83`). For a pod started by digest, k3s/containerd reports that field as the bare image ID (`sha256:<config>`). Both scanners then try to pull `docker.io/library/sha256:<id>`, and their own stderr shows the refusal (`UNAUTHORIZED ... Name:library/sha256`). They exit 1, and the scanner logs "scan failed, image skipped" (`scanner_exit`).
- **Experiment, run on the cluster above:**
  - `nginx@sha256:65645c...` reported `status.image` as `sha256:6769dc...`, and the scan failed.
  - `busybox:1.36`, started by tag, scanned.
- **Reach:** the `javv-scanner` chart pins its own images by digest, so no install ever scans its own two scanner images: each cycle skips at least its own pod. Pinning workloads by digest is common supply-chain practice.
- **The data needed for a fix is already there:** `image_id` holds a pullable `repo@sha256:...`.
- **Open question:** other runtimes are not tested.

### 3. Three settings pages never load before the first cluster (medium)

- **Pages:** Scan scope, Scanning, and the retention block of Data & OpenSearch.
- **Why:** each loads in a watch on the selected cluster that returns when there is none, so `loading` stays true. See `ScanScopeView.vue:49`, `ScanningView.vue:60` and `DataOpenSearchView.vue:102`.
- **Evidence:** the browser's network log, after 30 s and 20 s on the page, shows no settings read at all. The only calls are `auth/me`, `meta`, `notifications` and `clusters`, which returned an empty list.
- **Unaffected:** Tokens, Users & roles, SLA policy and Cluster load correctly.

### 4. A skipped image disappears from the UI without a sign (medium)

- **The rule behind it:** the scanner certifies the inventory with the scanned images only. That is by design (issue 633, `scanner/src/scanner/run.py:115-123`), and this finding does not question it.
- **The gap:** the cycle's `scan_failed` count is written only to the scanner pod's log.
- **Seen live:** 6 images were running and Running images showed 4. Scanner status showed both scanners healthy, with no failed ingests.
- **Why it is worse with finding 2:** together they hide every digest-pinned workload.
- **Question:** should the skipped count reach the backend and show on Scanner status?

### 5. A refused findings search reads as "no findings" (medium)

When the per-user search budget is used up (429), Findings shows all of these at once:
- the alert "The search backend is busy. Try again in a few seconds.";
- the header "0 findings";
- the grid's cold-start line "No findings yet. The first committed scan populates this grid.";
- the facets beside it, which still count 508 open.

This is the same family as #749: a failed read shown as a real result.

The 429 came from back-to-back smoke runs at the default limit of 10. `docs/CONFIGURATION.md` says the smoke needs 50. Whether a person can reach the limit belongs to area 4.

### 6. Behind a firewall that drops packets, every page load is blank for about 22 s (medium)

`frontend/index.html` loads the two fonts from Google Fonts as a render-blocking stylesheet, and the app's script waits for it. Measured with a browser whose resolver points the two font hosts at a failing target:

| Network | Sign-in visible after | Fonts |
|---|---|---|
| Online | 1.1 s | Hanken Grotesk, Space Mono |
| DNS fails (an internal Docker network) | 0.35 s | fallback |
| Unroutable address (a firewall that drops packets) | 21.8 s | fallback |

- **Fallback fonts:** they read well. This was already expected in the issue.
- **The server side is clean offline:**
  - the backend makes no outbound calls;
  - all three containers were healthy;
  - the only warning is the documented demo-certificate one.

### 7. Two installs on one host share one compose project (low)

`compose.yaml` sets `name: javv`. A second install in another folder, made by following the docs, takes over the first install's containers and volumes. `docs/DEPLOYING.md` does not say so.

### 8. The empty-state action is a button inside a link (low)

- **Where:** `frontend/src/layouts/AppShell.vue:146-148`, `<RouterLink class="es-link"><UiButton>`.
- **Problem:** these are nested interactive controls, so keyboard focus stops twice for one action. Walked: account menu, then the link, then the button.

### 9. The primary button gives no feedback on a press (design, needs a ruling)

- **Report:** "Create a scanner token" feels flat on a click.
- **Scope:** `UiButton variant="primary"` is shared, so the change is a DESIGN.md §8.5 ruling for every primary button.
- **Specimens:** A to E were built on the live stack, each keeping the flat coral of 2026-07-17 at rest:
  - **A, push:** sinks 1px and shrinks to 97% on press.
  - **B, pressed in:** darker, with an inner shade.
  - **C, lift:** rises on hover with a coral shadow.
  - **D, ring:** a coral ring on press.
  - **E:** A and D together.
- **Status:** waiting for the ruling.

## Next

- **Fixes:** each one goes in its own PR after this triage.
- **Area 2 is not complete yet:** the Helm install and the upgrade runs (area 3) follow, then areas 6 and 4.

items.body:
Jira Link: [DB-24321](https://yugabyte.atlassian.net/browse/DB-24321)
### Description

**What happened**

We ran a plain database-wide `ANALYZE` (statement_timeout 0) on YugabyteDB 2026.1.2.0-b137. The small tables finished in seconds. The big one (about 2.2 TB per copy, 523M rows, ~161 tablets, RF3) ran for 26.5 minutes and then failed:

    ERROR:  Snapshot too old. Read point: { physical: 1791669311224496 }, earliest read time allowed: { physical: 1791669394550547 }, delta (usec): 83.326s. ... kSnapshotTooOld

The read point was taken about 5 minutes into that table, so the #27437 fix (a fresh read time after block selection) did kick in. But the second phase alone then ran for over 21 minutes. That's past the default 15-minute history retention (`timestamp_history_retention_interval_sec=900`), and it missed by 83 seconds.

The cluster was nearly idle during the run (1.7–3.5 cores in use across 6 tservers, for the 19 minutes we could monitor), so this isn't a heavy-load problem.

**Expected**

ANALYZE completes on a table this size with default settings. Failing that, it should refresh its read point during phase 2, or fail early with a clear message about the limit.

**Environment**

- 2026.1.2.0-b137 (contains the #27437 backport fc9d652bdf55)
- 6 tservers, RF3, Kubernetes (GKE)
- block-based sampling, default_statistics_target 100

**Workaround**

Raise `timestamp_history_retention_interval_sec` (it's a runtime flag) above the expected ANALYZE time, run ANALYZE, then set it back.

Related: #27437 (fix present but not enough at this size), #27483 (ANALYZE on very large tables takes ~30 min).
