items.title: Deploy metrics-server via ArgoCD (Talos add-on; enables kubectl top + HPAs + descheduler real-usage)

labels.name: jeeves
labels.description: Jeeves: autonomously plan, code and PR this ticket

items.body:
## Goal

Deploy **metrics-server** as a first-class ArgoCD app. Talos ships no metrics-server and this GitOps repo has never declared one, so `kubectl top` fails cluster-wide, the `v1beta1.metrics.k8s.io` APIService is absent, HPAs can't function, and the descheduler can't read real node usage. Add it via GitOps following the existing app pattern.

## Desired end state / acceptance criteria

- `metrics-server` runs in namespace `kube-system`, managed by ArgoCD (automated sync, selfHeal, prune).
- `kubectl get apiservice v1beta1.metrics.k8s.io` → `AVAILABLE=True`.
- `kubectl top nodes` returns real CPU/memory for all 5 nodes; `kubectl top pods -A` works.
- ArgoCD Application `metrics-server` is Synced + Healthy.

## Files to create/change — follow the existing descheduler app pattern exactly

Reference templates already in the repo: `cluster/argocd/apps/descheduler.yaml` (multi-source Helm Application) and `cluster/apps/descheduler/values.yaml` (Helm values). Mirror that structure.

1. **CREATE `cluster/argocd/apps/metrics-server.yaml`** — an ArgoCD `Application`, multi-source like `descheduler.yaml`:
   - Helm chart `metrics-server` from repo `https://kubernetes-sigs.github.io/metrics-server/`.
   - `targetRevision`: **pin** to the current latest stable chart version from that repo's `index.yaml` (do NOT use `latest`/unpinned — repo rule).
   - Second source = this repo (`https://github.com/Arsenikki/kuberseni-gitops`, `main`) with `ref: values`; `valueFiles: [$values/cluster/apps/metrics-server/values.yaml]`.
   - `project: kuberseni`, destination namespace `kube-system`.
   - `syncPolicy.automated` with `prune: true`, `selfHeal: true`; `syncOptions`: `CreateNamespace=true`, `ServerSideApply=true`.
   - Add a sync-wave annotation earlier than its consumers (e.g. `argocd.argoproj.io/sync-wave: "1"`) so metrics are available before the descheduler run.
   - `root-app.yaml` recurses `cluster/argocd/` and will auto-discover this file — no extra registration needed.

2. **CREATE `cluster/apps/metrics-server/values.yaml`** — Helm values with the **Talos-required** kubelet TLS workaround (see below) plus modest requests.

3. **EDIT `cluster/argocd/projects/kuberseni.yaml`** — add `https://kubernetes-sigs.github.io/metrics-server/` to `spec.sourceRepos`. **REQUIRED**: the `kuberseni` AppProject whitelists source repos; without this the app is blocked with "application repo … is not permitted to be used".

## Talos-specific REQUIRED config (classic gotcha)

Talos kubelet serving certificates are self-signed, so metrics-server's default TLS verification against the kubelet fails with x509 errors and `kubectl top` returns no data. In `values.yaml` set:

```yaml
args:
  - --kubelet-insecure-tls
  - --kubelet-preferred-address-types=InternalIP
replicas: 1
resources:
  requests:
```

items.body:
### Is there an existing issue for this?

- [x] I have searched the existing issues

### Version

equal or higher than v1.19.8 and lower than v1.20.0

### What happened?

When creating multiple routes (HTTPRoute/GRPCRoute) pointing to the same Service but with different `parentRef.port` values, Cilium merges all of them into a single Envoy listener and a single `listener-insecure` RouteConfiguration, regardless of their target port. Routes from different ports share one virtual host (`*`), and rules with identical matches (e.g. both with no `matches`) are even aggregated into one Envoy route with the backends of both routes combined.

**Expected behavior:** Routes with explicit `parentRef.port` should be isolated. An HTTPRoute targeting port 9090 and a GRPCRoute targeting port 9091 on the same Service should produce separate routing domains (either separate CECs or separate Envoy listeners/RouteConfigurations).

**Actual behavior:** Both routes are merged into the single `listener-insecure` RouteConfiguration of the Service's CEC. With the reproduction below (no `matches` on either route), both rules end up in **one** Envoy route whose weighted clusters contain the backends of both routes (`sample-stable:9090` w80, `sample-canary:9090` w20, `sample-stable:9091` w100, `sample-canary:9091` w0), so traffic on either port is split across both backend ports. If the matches differ, the first sorted match wins across ports instead.

### How can we reproduce the issue?

**TLDR:**

1. Create a Service exposing two ports (e.g., 9090 for HTTP, 9091 for gRPC)
2. Create an HTTPRoute with `parentRef` pointing to the Service on port 9090
3. Create a GRPCRoute with `parentRef` pointing to the same Service on port 9091
4. Observe the generated CiliumEnvoyConfig both routes are merged into a single CEC

**Minimal Reproduction:**

For context, this was for:
- testing GAMMA with Argo Rollouts, but it shouldn't matter as Argo Rollouts only touches the weights of the routes.
- having different routes pointing to the same service/pods, with both HTTP and gRPC.

Keeping minimal manifest here (omitting the `backendRefs` services.

```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: sample
spec:
  selector:
    app: sample-server
  ports:
  - name: http
    port: 9090
    protocol: TCP
  - name: grpc
    port: 9091
    protocol: TCP
    appProtocol: kubernetes.io/h2c
---
apiVersion: gateway.networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: GRPCRoute
metadata:
  name: sample-grpc
spec:
  parentRefs:
  - group: ''
    kind: Service
    name: sample
    port: 9091
  rules:
  - backendRefs:
    - group: ''
      name: sample-stable
      port: 9091
      weight: 100
    - group: ''
      name: sample-canary
      port: 9091
      weight: 0
---
apiVersion: gateway.networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: HTTPRoute
metadata:
  name: sample-http
spec:
  parentRefs:
  - group: ''
    kind: Service
    name: sample
    port: 9090
  rules:
  - backendRefs:
    - group: ''
      name: sample-stable
      port: 9090
      weight: 80
    - group: ''
      name: sample-canary
      port: 9090
      weight: 20
```

---

Resulting CEC, cropping to the part where I think it becomes problematic

```yaml
apiVersion: cilium.io/v2
kind: CiliumEnvoyConfig
metadata:
  ...
  name: sample
  ...
spec:
  ...
  resources:
  ...
  - '@type': type.googleapis.com/envoy.config.route.v3.RouteConfiguration
    name: listener-insecure
    virtualHosts:
    - domains:
      - '*'
      name: '*'
      routes:
      - match:
          prefix: /
        route:
          maxStreamDuration:
            maxStreamDuration: 0s
          weightedClusters:
            clusters:
            - name: iss:sample-stable:9090
              weight: 80
            - name: iss:sample-canary:9090
              weight: 20
      - match:
          prefix: /
        route:
          maxStreamDuration:
            maxStreamDuration: 0s
          weightedClusters:
            clusters:
            - name: iss:sample-stable:9091
              weight: 100
            - name: iss:sample-canary:9091
              weight: 0
  ...
```

**Result:** Single CEC `demo-grpc` with both routes merged into `listener-insecure` RouteConfiguration. gRPC traffic on 9091 incorrectly matches the `/` prefix rule from the HTTPRoute.


### Cilium Version

Client: 1.19.6 9a898243 2026-07-16T13:44:52+00:00 go version go1.25.12 linux/arm64
Daemon: 1.19.6 9a898243 2026-07-16T13:44:52+00:00 go version go1.25.12 linux/arm64

I checked the code in several branches and this behavior seems to be the case.

### Kernel Version

6.12.88-119.157.amzn2023.aarch64

### Kubernetes Version

v1.34.10-eks-cb19647

### Regression

_No response_

### Sysdump

_No response_

### Relevant log output

```shell

```

### Anything else?

### Relevant Code References

These are LLM assisted findings.

---

The bug spans multiple layers in the GAMMA translation pipeline:

| Layer | File | Issue |
|-------|------|-------|
| Ingestion | `operator/pkg/model/ingestion/gamma.go` | ✓ Correctly creates separate HTTPListener per port: `ns-svc-9090`, `ns-svc-9091` |
| Route Config | `operator/pkg/model/translation/envoy_route_configuration.go:39` | ✗ All non-TLS routes keyed by constant `insecureHost` → single RouteConfiguration / virtual host for all ports |
| Route aggregation | `operator/pkg/model/translation/envoy_virtual_host.go:370-387` | ✗ Routes with the same match key (`GetBackendAggregationKey()` falls back to `GetMatchKey()`) are merged into one Envoy route, combining backends from routes attached to different ports |
| Listener / CEC Translator | `operator/pkg/model/translation/envoy_listener.go`, `cec_translator.go` | ✗ All plaintext HTTP ports share one Envoy listener (`listener`) and one `ServiceListener`. Even the per-port path (`NeedsPerPortListeners()`) only splits HTTPS / TLS passthrough ports, not plaintext HTTP |

Note: the CEC being named after the Service only (`translator.go:93-95`) is not itself a cause — one CEC per Service is fine as long as it contains per-port listeners and RouteConfigurations.

**Key code excerpts:**

```go
// envoy_route_configuration.go:39 — All GAMMA routes collapse to same key
port := insecureHost  // constant for all non-TLS; only TLS gets port-specific keying

// envoy_virtual_host.go:371-375 — identical matches from different routes are aggregated
key := r.GetBackendAggregationKey()  // "path:|" for both routes in the repro
matchBackendMap[key] = append(matchBackendMap[key], r)

// envoy_listener.go:414-470 / cec_translator.go:208-224 — even in per-port mode,
// all plaintext HTTP ports go to the shared `listener` / `listener-insecure`
```

---

Some permalinks for reference:

https://github.com/cilium/cilium/blob/759307f9f98738bdc7be302a4f329183b70fae77/operator/pkg/model/translation/envoy_virtual_host.go#L370-L387


https://github.com/cilium/cilium/blob/550f48dd22f3f2b560f8fa53ffabfd4933ea4d6f/operator/pkg/model/translation/envoy_route_configuration.go#L39

https://github.com/cilium/cilium/blob/550f48dd22f3f2b560f8fa53ffabfd4933ea4d6f/operator/pkg/model/translation/gateway-api/translator.go#L92-L95

### Workarounds

I tested several workarounds to avoid this issue.

#### 1. Use separate Services per port

Split the multi-port Service into separate single-port Services. Since the CEC is keyed by Service name, each Service gets its own CEC with isolated routing.

```yaml
# Instead of one Service with ports 9090 and 9091:
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: demo-http
spec:
  ports:
  - name: http
    port: 9090
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: demo-grpc
spec:
  ports:
  - name: grpc
    port: 9091
    appProtocol: kubernetes.io/h2c
```

Then point HTTPRoute to `demo-http` and GRPCRoute to `demo-grpc`. Each generates its own CEC with no route collision. Though this way we have multiple hostnames pointing to essentially the same thing.

### 2. Add explicit matches to disambiguate routes

I tried adding explicit `matches` filters to disambiguate at the route level, especially for the GRPCRoute to denote that this accepts a certain method prefix.

```yaml
# GRPCRoute with explicit method matching (translated to Envoy regex `/echo.*/.+`)
spec:
  rules:
  - matches:
    - method:
        type: RegularExpression
        service: "echo.*"
    backendRefs:
    - name: sample-stable
      port: 9091
```

This forces route-level disambiguation but is not a proper fix.

### Suggested Fix

Emit one Envoy Listener + RouteConfiguration per plaintext HTTP port within the Service's CEC (same approach as #44889 for HTTPS/TLS, and as proposed for Gateways in #47551):

1. Key GAMMA route configurations by listener port (`listener-<port>`) instead of the `insecureHost` constant, with a matching HCM/RDS name per port.
2. Emit one `ServiceListener` per port with `Listener` set, so each Service port is redirected to its own Envoy listener (supported since #45949).
3. Use the actual listener port instead of `m.HTTP[0].Port` for redirect `ListenerPort` (`envoy_route_configuration.go:145,167`).

items.title: Deletes are not crash-consistent: a kill mid-delete leaves objects that are neither visible nor deletable
items.body:
### Supported storage confirmation

- [X] I have reproduced this issue with all RustFS data directories on supported storage (local disks, SAN/Fibre Channel, or JBOD; XFS recommended), without NFS, SMB/Samba/CIFS, or other remote or shared filesystem mounts, including storage backing Docker volumes and Kubernetes PersistentVolumes.

### Describe the bug

A server process can stop at any instruction: power loss, OOM kill, pod restart, `kill -9`. After such a stop every object in a bucket should be in one of two states: present and readable, or absent. Object deletion does not give that guarantee. A process killed in the middle of `DeleteObjects` (or `DeleteObject`) leaves objects on disk that are in neither state:

- `xl.meta` is gone, so the object is not listed and `HEAD` returns 404;
- a repeated `DeleteObjects`/`DeleteObject` for the key returns `<Deleted>`/204 and changes nothing on disk;
- non-force `DeleteBucket` returns `409 BucketNotEmpty` although `ListObjectsV2` reports `KeyCount=0`;
- the scanner, the empty-listing orphan purge (#7955, #8261), `heal` (including the erasure-set heal that runs after an unclean shutdown) and a restart do not finish or revert them.

Nothing in the server ever brings these objects to "present" or to "absent". The only way out is removing the directories by hand with the server stopped.

**What #8374 / #8378 covered and what they did not.** #8378 (merged, `main` only, not in 1.0.1) made the delete survive a client disconnect and reclaims residue that carries a committed `delete-data.<T>` marker. It explicitly leaves two shapes alone, and a process kill produces both on current `main`:

- **(b) reserved, not committed**: no `xl.meta`; the data dir still holds `part.N` and `reserve-delete-data.<T>`; `<T>/xl.meta.bkp` next to it. The kill landed after `xl.meta` was removed and before the marker was renamed to `delete-data.<T>`.
- **(c) backup only**: no `xl.meta`, no data dir, just `<key>/<T>/xl.meta.bkp`. For inline objects (data inside `xl.meta`, default threshold 128 KiB) this is what a kill between the commit and the cleanup pass leaves; for non-inline objects it is a kill inside the cleanup pass after the data dir went.

Both shapes are in the wild: the 7051 `xl.meta.bkp` files of #6898 (median 6.6 KB, so mostly inline objects; 154 MB in total) are (c), and the one directory there with `part.1` plus `reserve-delete-data.<T>` is (b). #8335 hides them from listings; it does not remove them.

**Why they cannot simply be deleted.** Shape (c) is ambiguous. The same `<key>/<T>/xl.meta.bkp` without `xl.meta` is also what an interrupted *rollback* leaves: when the write quorum fails, every online disk runs `restore_delete_rollback`, which first removes the delete markers from the data dirs and only then renames `<T>/xl.meta.bkp` back to `xl.meta` ([local.rs#L338-L405](https://github.com/rustfs/rustfs/blob/a424d10fa0317a1fd973c1cdae77db85adc5263b/crates/ecstore/src/disk/local.rs#L338-L405), markers at [#L345](https://github.com/rustfs/rustfs/blob/a424d10fa0317a1fd973c1cdae77db85adc5263b/crates/ecstore/src/disk/local.rs#L345), rename at [#L369-L370](https://github.com/rustfs/rustfs/blob/a424d10fa0317a1fd973c1cdae77db85adc5263b/crates/ecstore/src/disk/local.rs#L369-L370)). A kill between those two steps leaves a backup that must be restored, not removed; a kill after a committed inline delete leaves a backup that must be removed. On one disk the two cases look identical, so the decision needs more than the local directory (the other disks of the set, or a policy). This is why I am filing it as a design question rather than a patch.

### Steps to reproduce

Single node, single drive, `main` at `a424d10fa` (release build, includes #8378). Full script and all eight runs under the spoiler.

1. Create a bucket, upload 1000 inline objects (4 KiB) and 1000 non-inline objects (1 MiB).
2. Send four `DeleteObjects` requests of 500 keys each in parallel (inline and non-inline keys interleaved).
3. `kill -9` the `rustfs` process 0.1 to 1.0 s later.
4. Start it again, wait for the unclean-shutdown heal to complete, then: `ListObjectsV2`, `DeleteObjects` for all 2000 keys again, an empty recursive listing (triggers the orphan purge), `DeleteBucket`.
5. Classify every object directory on the drive that has no `xl.meta`.

Result (kill after 0.5 s): right after the kill 343 objects are in shape (c), 347 carry a committed marker, 1310 are intact. After the restart and the retry, the 347 committed ones and the 1310 intact ones are gone (#8378 works as described), the 343 (c) objects are still there, `ListObjectsV2` says `KeyCount=0`, `DeleteBucket` says `409 BucketNotEmpty`. Shape (c) appeared in 8 of 8 runs (11 to 825 objects, all inline); shape (b) in 1 of 8 (one 1 MiB object, kill after 0.7 s), and it also survived restart, retry and listing.

<details>
<summary>Script, how to run it, and the eight runs</summary>

Requirements: bash, curl >= 7.75 (`--aws-sigv4`), openssl; a single-drive RustFS whose volume directory is readable; the script kills the process by PID and asks you to start it again.

```bash
EP=http://127.0.0.1:9000 AK=... SK=... VOL=<RUSTFS_VOLUMES dir> PID=$(pgrep -x rustfs) KILL_AFTER=0.5 ./kill-repro.sh prepare
#   -> uploads, sends the deletes, kills the process, prints the on-disk state
<start rustfs again, wait ~20 s>
EP=... AK=... SK=... VOL=... ./kill-repro.sh check
#   -> listing, retry DeleteObjects, empty listing, DeleteBucket, on-disk state
```

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Reproduces: a rustfs process killed in the middle of DeleteObjects leaves objects without xl.meta
# that no later operation finishes or reverts (shapes "backup only" and "reserved marker").
set -u
EP=${EP:?}; AK=${AK:?}; SK=${SK:?}; VOL=${VOL:?}
BUCKET=${BUCKET:-kill-repro}; N_SMALL=${N_SMALL:-1000}; N_LARGE=${N_LARGE:-1000}; BATCH=${BATCH:-500}
export EP AK SK BUCKET
s3() { curl -sS --aws-sigv4 "aws:amz:us-east-1:s3" --user "$AK:$SK" -H 'x-amz-content-sha256: UNSIGNED-PAYLOAD' "$@"; }
export -f s3
W=${W:-/tmp/kill-repro}; mkdir -p "$W"; export W

classify() { # object directories without xl.meta, by shape
	find "$VOL/$BUCKET" -mindepth 2 -maxdepth 2 -type d -name 'obj-*' | while read -r o; do
		[ -e "$o/xl.meta" ] && continue
		if   [ -n "$(find "$o" -name 'delete-data.*' -print -quit)" ]; then echo committed_marker
		elif [ -n "$(find "$o" -name 'reserve-delete-data.*' -print -quit)" ]; then echo reserved_marker
		elif [ -n "$(find "$o" -name xl.meta.bkp -print -quit)" ]; then echo backup_only
		else echo other; fi
	done | sort | uniq -c | tr -s ' \n' '  '; echo
}
state() {
	local d="$VOL/$BUCKET"
	printf '%-24s xl.meta=%-5s xl.meta.bkp=%-5s part.*=%-5s delete-data.*=%-4s reserve-delete-data.*=%-3s listed=%s\n' "$1" \
		"$(find "$d" -name xl.meta | wc -l)" "$(find "$d" -name xl.meta.bkp | wc -l)" "$(find "$d" -name 'part.*' | wc -l)" \
		"$(find "$d" -name 'delete-data.*' | wc -l)" "$(find "$d" -name 'reserve-delete-data.*' | wc -l)" "${2:--}"
}
listed() { # root page KeyCount (continuation tokens break curl's SigV4 canonicalisation; keep <= 1000 keys per prefix)
	local t=0; for p in small large; do t=$((t + $(s3 "$EP/$BUCKET?list-type=2&max-keys=1000&prefix=$p" | grep -o '<KeyCount>[0-9]*' | cut -d'>' -f2))); done; echo $t
}
delete_batch() { # delete_batch <keys-file> <out-prefix>
	local xml="$2.xml"; { printf '<Delete><Quiet>true</Quiet>'; while read -r k; do printf '<Object><Key>%s</Key></Object>' "$k"; done < "$1"; printf '</Delete>'; } > "$xml"
	s3 -o "$2.resp" -w '%{http_code}\n' -X POST "$EP/$BUCKET?delete=" -H "Content-MD5: $(openssl md5 -binary "$xml" | base64)" -H 'Content-Type: application/xml' --data-binary @"$xml" 2>/dev/null
}
export -f delete_batch

case ${1:?prepare|check} in
prepare)
	PID=${PID:?pid of the rustfs process}; KILL_AFTER=${KILL_AFTER:-0.5}
	head -c 4096 /dev/urandom > "$W/small"; head -c $((1024*1024)) /dev/urandom > "$W/large"
	echo "create bucket: $(s3 -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' -X PUT "$EP/$BUCKET")"
	seq -f 'small/obj-%05g.bin' 1 "$N_SMALL" > "$W/keys.small"; seq -f 'large/obj-%05g.bin' 1 "$N_LARGE" > "$W/keys.large"
	for k in small large; do xargs -P 16 -I{} bash -c "s3 -o /dev/null -X PUT \"\$EP/\$BUCKET/{}\" --data-binary @\"\$W/$k\"" < "$W/keys.$k"; done
	paste -d'\n' "$W/keys.large" "$W/keys.small" | sed '/^$/d' > "$W/keys.all"; sort -u "$W/keys.all" > "$W/keys.sorted"
	rm -f "$W"/batch.*; split -l "$BATCH" -d -a 3 "$W/keys.all" "$W/batch."
	state "after upload" "$(listed)"
	ls "$W"/batch.??? | xargs -P 4 -I{} bash -c 'delete_batch {} {}.out' > "$W/codes" &
	sleep "$KILL_AFTER"; kill -9 "$PID"; wait
	echo "killed rustfs after ${KILL_AFTER}s; DeleteObjects HTTP codes: $(sort "$W/codes" | uniq -c | tr -s ' \n' '  ')"
	state "right after kill"; echo "residue: $(classify)"
	echo "unclean-shutdown marker: $(find "$VOL/.rustfs.sys" -name '*unclean*' | sed "s|$VOL/||")"
	echo ">>> start rustfs again, wait ~20 s, then: $0 check"
	;;
check)
	state "after restart" "$(listed)"; echo "residue: $(classify)"
	rm -f "$W"/retry.*; split -l 1000 -d -a 3 "$W/keys.sorted" "$W/retry."
	for f in "$W"/retry.???; do delete_batch "$f" "$f.out"; done > "$W/retry.codes"
	echo "retry DeleteObjects (all keys): HTTP $(sort "$W/retry.codes" | uniq -c | tr -s ' \n' '  '), <Deleted>=$(cat "$W"/retry.*.out.resp | grep -o '<Deleted>' | wc -l), <Error>=$(cat "$W"/retry.*.out.resp | grep -o '<Error>' | wc -l)"
	sleep 5; state "5s after retry" "$(listed)"; echo "residue: $(classify)"
	s3 -o /dev/null "$EP/$BUCKET?list-type=2&max-keys=1000"; sleep 5   # empty recursive listing -> orphan purge
	state "after empty listing" "$(listed)"; echo "residue: $(classify)"
	echo "DeleteBucket: HTTP $(s3 -o "$W/db.xml" -w '%{http_code}' -X DELETE "$EP/$BUCKET") $(grep -o '<Code>[^<]*' "$W/db.xml" | cut -d'>' -f2)"
	o=$(find "$VOL/$BUCKET" -name 'reserve-delete-data.*' -o -name xl.meta.bkp | head -1 | xargs -r dirname | xargs -r dirname)
	[ -n "$o" ] && { echo "example: ${o#"$VOL/"}"; find "$o" -mindepth 1 -printf '  %P %s B\n'; }
	;;
esac
```

Eight runs on `main` `a424d10fa` (release build, ext4, single drive; the first seven with a longer variant of the script, the last one with the script above). `committed` = `delete-data.<T>` present, finished by the retry; `live+leftovers` = `xl.meta` still present with a `<T>/` dir or a `reserve-delete-data.<T>` next to it, deleted normally by the retry.

| mix small/large | kill after | right after the kill (objects without `xl.meta`) | after restart + retry + empty listing | DeleteBucket |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1000/1000 | 0.1 s | 11 backup_only (small), 6 committed (large), 2 live+leftovers | 11 backup_only | 409 |
| 1000/1000 | 0.3 s | 158 backup_only, 165 committed, 3 live+leftovers | 158 backup_only | 409 |
| 1000/1000 | 0.5 s | 351 backup_only, 324 committed, 2 live+leftovers | 351 backup_only | 409 |
| 1000/1000 | 1.0 s | 825 backup_only, 827 committed | 825 backup_only | 409 |
| 200/1800 | 0.3 s | 12 backup_only, 100 committed, 2 live+leftovers | 12 backup_only | 409 |
| 200/1800 | 0.5 s | 60 backup_only, 338 committed, 4 live+leftovers | 60 backup_only | 409 |
| 200/1800 | 0.7 s | 95 backup_only, 542 committed, **1 reserved_marker** (large), 3 live+leftovers | 95 backup_only + **1 reserved_marker** | 409 |
| 1000/1000 | 0.5 s | 343 backup_only, 347 committed, 3 live+leftovers | 343 backup_only | 409 |

Output of the last run (script above, kill after 0.5 s):

```
create bucket: 200
after upload             xl.meta=2000  xl.meta.bkp=0     part.*=1000  delete-data.*=0    reserve-delete-data.*=0   listed=2000
killed rustfs after 0.5s; DeleteObjects HTTP codes:  4 000
right after kill         xl.meta=1310  xl.meta.bkp=693   part.*=1000  delete-data.*=347  reserve-delete-data.*=3   listed=-
residue:  343 backup_only 347 committed_marker
unclean-shutdown marker: .rustfs.sys/unclean-shutdown
>>> start rustfs again, wait ~20 s, then: ./kill-repro.sh check
   (server log: "Unclean shutdown detected; scheduling erasure-set heal for local sets" ... "Heal task completed", 0.9 s later)
after restart            xl.meta=1310  xl.meta.bkp=690   part.*=1000  delete-data.*=347  reserve-delete-data.*=3   listed=1310
residue:  343 backup_only 347 committed_marker
retry DeleteObjects (all keys): HTTP  2 200 , <Deleted>=2000, <Error>=0
5s after retry           xl.meta=0     xl.meta.bkp=343   part.*=0     delete-data.*=0    reserve-delete-data.*=0   listed=0
residue:  343 backup_only
after empty listing      xl.meta=0     xl.meta.bkp=343   part.*=0     delete-data.*=0    reserve-delete-data.*=0   listed=0
residue:  343 backup_only
DeleteBucket: HTTP 409 BucketNotEmpty
example: kill-repro/small/obj-00075.bin
  b5ef5538-018d-4dfd-8861-4803a7672b17 4096 B
  b5ef5538-018d-4dfd-8861-4803a7672b17/xl.meta.bkp 4690 B
```

(The 3 `reserve-delete-data.*` right after the kill belong to objects that still have `xl.meta`; they go away with the retry. The 693 → 690 `xl.meta.bkp` drop across the restart is their `<T>/xl.meta.bkp` disappearing next to live metadata while the reserved markers stay; I did not trace what removes them.)

The one shape (b) object (0.7 s run), same layout as the one in #6898:

```
kill-repro/large/obj-01367.bin/
├── b9ebc787-e396-44eb-8654-49796010e961/              <- rollback dir T
│   └── xl.meta.bkp                                     493 B
└── 1a7fb848-bb6e-4882-a163-f55f35022555/              <- data dir
    ├── part.1                                          1048608 B
    └── reserve-delete-data.b9ebc787-e396-44eb-8654-49796010e961   0 B
```

Server log on `DeleteBucket` for that run: `"event":"bucket_delete_blocked" ... "blocker":"orphan_directory","files":98,"uuid_data_dirs":97,"sample":"large/obj-01367.bin/1a7fb848-…/reserve-delete-data.b9ebc787-…"`.

</details>

### Expected behavior

After any process stop, every object is either fully present or fully absent, and the server gets there on its own: at the latest on the next start after an unclean shutdown, or on the next operation that touches the key. Concretely, for the two shapes above, either the delete is rolled forward (the residue is removed and the space returned) or rolled back (`xl.meta` restored from `<T>/xl.meta.bkp`, markers removed) — but never left in a state that `ListObjects`, `DeleteObject(s)`, `heal` and `DeleteBucket` all refuse to touch.

### RustFS version

`main` at `a424d10fa0317a1fd973c1cdae77db85adc5263b` (release build, includes #8378, which is not in any tagged release yet). 1.0.0 shows the same two shapes plus the committed shape that #8378 now finishes (#8374); 1.0.1 predates #8378. #6898 is 1.0.0-era residue.

### Deployment method

Binary

### Data directory filesystems and mounts

```
RustFS data paths: one volume under /mnt/data (RUSTFS_VOLUMES), single node, single drive
Filesystem types and mount sources: ext4 on a local block device (no NFS/SMB/overlay)
Mount command output:
TARGET    SOURCE    FSTYPE OPTIONS
/mnt/data /dev/sdb1 ext4   rw,noatime
Docker host paths or Kubernetes volume backing storage: not applicable
```

### Server operating system and architecture

Debian 12 (bookworm), x86_64

### Client environment

curl 7.88.1 with `--aws-sigv4` (script above). In the field: any S3 client that batch-deletes while the server is restarted or OOM-killed (#6898: OpenObserve on Kubernetes).

### Relevant logs

```shell
# startup after the kill: the unclean-shutdown heal runs and completes without touching the residue
{"level":"INFO","message":"Unclean shutdown detected; scheduling erasure-set heal for local sets","event":"heal_unclean_shutdown","set_count":1,...}
{"level":"INFO","message":"Heal task started","event":"heal_task_state","heal_type":"erasure_set","state":"started",...}
{"level":"INFO","message":"Heal task completed","event":"heal_task_state","heal_type":"erasure_set","state":"completed",...}
# DeleteBucket afterwards
{"level":"ERROR","message":"Bucket deletion was blocked by residue the client cannot reach through the S3 API","event":"bucket_delete_blocked","bucket":"kill-repro","blocker":"orphan_directory","files":343,"uuid_data_dirs":343,"sample":"small/obj-00477.bin/e3e6eb6a-9c33-42f2-a357-b9fdd0e7d554/xl.meta.bkp",...}
```

### Screenshots

_No response_

### Additional context

All links are to `main` at `a424d10fa`.

#### Where the shapes come from

Per object and disk, `delete_versions_internal` does: write `<key>/<T>/xl.meta.bkp` ([local.rs#L7357](https://github.com/rustfs/rustfs/blob/a424d10fa0317a1fd973c1cdae77db85adc5263b/crates/ecstore/src/disk/local.rs#L7357)); create `reserve-delete-data.<T>` in the data dir, skipped when there is none, i.e. inline ([#L7474-L7495](https://github.com/rustfs/rustfs/blob/a424d10fa0317a1fd973c1cdae77db85adc5263b/crates/ecstore/src/disk/local.rs#L7474-L7495), [#L9183-L9187](https://github.com/rustfs/rustfs/blob/a424d10fa0317a1fd973c1cdae77db85adc5263b/crates/ecstore/src/disk/local.rs#L9183-L9187)); remove `xl.meta` ([#L7568-L7572](https://github.com/rustfs/rustfs/blob/a424d10fa0317a1fd973c1cdae77db85adc5263b/crates/ecstore/src/disk/local.rs#L7568-L7572)); rename the marker to `delete-data.<T>`, the commit point ([#L7604-L7608](https://github.com/rustfs/rustfs/blob/a424d10fa0317a1fd973c1cdae77db85adc5263b/crates/ecstore/src/disk/local.rs#L7604-L7608), [#L9226-L9263](https://github.com/rustfs/rustfs/blob/a424d10fa0317a1fd973c1cdae77db85adc5263b/crates/ecstore/src/disk/local.rs#L9226-L9263)). The set then either runs the cleanup pass (`delete("<key>/<T>")`, [ops/object.rs#L8814-L8838](https://github.com/rustfs/rustfs/blob/a424d10fa0317a1fd973c1cdae77db85adc5263b/crates/ecstore/src/set_disk/ops/object.rs#L8814-L8838)) or, on quorum failure, the rollback on every online disk ([#L8773-L8813](https://github.com/rustfs/rustfs/blob/a424d10fa0317a1fd973c1cdae77db85adc5263b/crates/ecstore/src/set_disk/ops/object.rs#L8773-L8813)). A kill between "remove `xl.meta`" and "rename marker" gives (b); between the commit and the end of cleanup gives (c) for inline objects (no data dir, no marker) and the committed shape for the others. A kill inside the rollback between "remove markers" and "rename backup back" gives (c) as well, with the opposite meaning.

#### Why nothing picks them up

- Repeated delete: a key without `xl.meta` runs `finish_committed_delete_residue`, which only acts on `delete-data.<T>` markers ([local.rs#L7325-L7331](https://github.com/rustfs/rustfs/blob/a424d10fa0317a1fd973c1cdae77db85adc5263b/crates/ecstore/src/disk/local.rs#L7325-L7331), [#L9353-L9407](https://github.com/rustfs/rustfs/blob/a424d10fa0317a1fd973c1cdae77db85adc5263b/crates/ecstore/src/disk/local.rs#L9353-L9407)), then returns `FileNotFound`; the handler reports not-found as `<Deleted>` ([delete.rs#L432-L451](https://github.com/rustfs/rustfs/blob/a424d10fa0317a1fd973c1cdae77db85adc5263b/rustfs/src/app/object/delete.rs#L432-L451)).
- Listing: `xl.meta.bkp`, `reserve-delete-data.*` and `part.N` count as residue and the directory is hidden ([local.rs#L178-L184](https://github.com/rustfs/rustfs/blob/a424d10fa0317a1fd973c1cdae77db85adc5263b/crates/ecstore/src/disk/local.rs#L178-L184), #8335).
- Empty-listing purge: a `<T>/xl.meta.bkp` is removed only when a data dir of the same object proves `T` committed, otherwise it blocks the whole chain; a data dir with `reserve-delete-data.*` blocks too ([io_primitives.rs#L5218-L5258](https://github.com/rustfs/rustfs/blob/a424d10fa0317a1fd973c1cdae77db85adc5263b/crates/ecstore/src/set_disk/core/io_primitives.rs#L5218-L5258)).
- Heal: metadata-less data dirs are reclaimed only with `--remove`, and only when they hold nothing but `part.N` and `delete-data.*` ([heal.rs#L965-L968](https://github.com/rustfs/rustfs/blob/a424d10fa0317a1fd973c1cdae77db85adc5263b/crates/ecstore/src/set_disk/ops/heal.rs#L965-L968), [#L2639-L2672](https://github.com/rustfs/rustfs/blob/a424d10fa0317a1fd973c1cdae77db85adc5263b/crates/ecstore/src/set_disk/ops/heal.rs#L2639-L2672)). The unclean-shutdown heal is an `ErasureSet` heal with default options, so `remove` is off ([unclean_shutdown.rs#L575-L590](https://github.com/rustfs/rustfs/blob/a424d10fa0317a1fd973c1cdae77db85adc5263b/crates/heal/src/heal/manager/unclean_shutdown.rs#L575-L590), [channel.rs#L820](https://github.com/rustfs/rustfs/blob/a424d10fa0317a1fd973c1cdae77db85adc5263b/crates/heal/src/heal/channel.rs#L820)), and its disk walk uses the same listing rule that hides the residue.
- `DeleteBucket`: non-force `delete_volume` removes empty directories only and fails closed on any file ([local.rs#L11362-L11384](https://github.com/rustfs/rustfs/blob/a424d10fa0317a1fd973c1cdae77db85adc5263b/crates/ecstore/src/disk/local.rs#L11362-L11384)); force (`x-rustfs-force-delete`, needs `ForceDeleteBucketAction`) removes the whole bucket tree, which is not a way to clear residue from a bucket that is in use.

#### Possible policies, for discussion

1. **Decide per object from the whole set, not one disk.** A `<T>` is safe to roll forward when any disk of the set holds `delete-data.<T>` for it, or when no disk holds `xl.meta` for the key and the request's quorum is met by disks without `xl.meta`; otherwise roll back (restore `xl.meta` from `<T>/xl.meta.bkp`, drop the markers). This is the same decision the delete itself makes, applied after the fact. It could run from `finish_committed_delete_residue` (then a repeated `DeleteObjects` of the keys would fix them), from the empty-listing purge, and from `heal`.
2. **A recovery pass at startup after an unclean shutdown**, since that is exactly when such residue is expected; the marker and the erasure-set heal already exist, the pass would apply policy 1 to every `<T>/xl.meta.bkp` and `reserve-delete-data.*` it finds.
3. **Age threshold** as an additional guard (a `<T>` older than, say, the lock lease cannot still be in flight), not as the sole criterion: it does not resolve the roll-forward vs roll-back question by itself.
4. **An admin command** (`heal --remove` extension, or a dedicated one) that applies policy 1 on demand and reports what it did, for volumes that already hold residue.

A cheaper preventive change for (c) on non-inline objects: in the cleanup pass remove `<T>/` before the marked data dirs, so an interruption keeps the marker as proof (as `finish_committed_delete_residue` already does for retries). It does not help inline objects, which have no marker at all.

#### Workaround

Stop the server and remove the object directories that have delete residue but no `xl.meta` (both shapes). Review the list before deleting: a key that is also a prefix of other keys (`a` next to `a/b`) must be skipped; on multi-drive deployments check every drive for `xl.meta` of the key before removing a shape (c) directory, since it may be an interrupted rollback.

```bash
VOL=<RUSTFS_VOLUMES dir>; BUCKET=<bucket>
sudo find "$VOL/$BUCKET" \( -name xl.meta.bkp -o -name 'reserve-delete-data.*' -o -name 'delete-data.*' \) -printf '%h\n' \
  | xargs -r -n1 dirname | sort -u | while read -r o; do [ -e "$o/xl.meta" ] || echo "$o"; done > /tmp/half-deleted.txt
wc -l /tmp/half-deleted.txt   # review, then remove with the server stopped
```

Related: #8374 (client disconnect, closed), #8378 (fix for the committed shape), #6898 (field report, both shapes), #8335 (hides them from listings).

items.body:
**Describe the bug**

Restoring a PVC from a LINSTOR `VolumeSnapshot` gives one replica with the data and two empty replicas, and all three are marked UpToDate. A pod that lands on an empty replica mounts a filesystem without the snapshot's files. This is silent data loss on restore: nothing fails up front, and a reader can see an empty volume before anything looks wrong.

**Environment**

- Cozystack main at `1d813c944`, plus the same main with the `piraeus-server` image rebuilt on Debian trixie (an open dependency roll-up). Both behave the same, so the base image is not the cause.
- Test cluster: three Talos nodes, kernel 6.18, DRBD 9.3.2, thick ZFS storage pool `data`.
- linstor-csi v1.11.2, LINSTOR 1.33.3, drbd-utils 9.34.3 (bookworm image) and 9.35.0 (trixie image).
- StorageClass `replicated` with `placementCount: "3"`, `storagePool: data`, `allowRemoteVolumeAccess: "true"`.

**To Reproduce**

1. Create a 1Gi RWO PVC on `replicated`, write a file from a pod, record its sha256, delete the pod.
2. Take a `VolumeSnapshot` with class `linstor-snapshots` and wait for `readyToUse`.
3. Create a PVC with `dataSource` set to the snapshot and a pod that reads the file.
4. Run `zfs get origin data/<pv>_00000` on each node and `linstor resource list --resources <pv>`.

**Expected behaviour**

All three replicas hold the snapshot's data, as clones or after a full resync from the restored replica, and the pod reads the same sha256.

**Actual behaviour**

Five restores out of five ended the same way, on both satellite images.

Only one node's zvol is a clone of the snapshot. On the other two nodes `origin` is `-`, so these are new empty zvols. The satellite on those nodes logs `DRBD meta data created for <pv>/0` and then `DRBD skipping initial sync for <pv>/0`. They come up UpToDate with a fresh UUID and nothing is resynced.

When the peers connect, the kernel logs `uuid_compare()=unrelated-data by rule=history-both` and `Unrelated data, aborting!`, and the connections go StandAlone. After that piraeus-ha-controller logs `resource '<pv>' on node '<node>' has failed, evicting` every minute and keeps deleting the VolumeAttachment. The node also gets the `drbd.linbit.com/lost-quorum:NoSchedule` taint, so nothing without a toleration is scheduled there until the volume is deleted.

In one run the reader pod got an empty replica:

```
sha256sum: can't open '/d/blob': No such file or directory
```

The snapshot itself is fine. I cloned the ZFS snapshot by hand on every node and read it with `drbdmeta ... internal dump-md`: the metadata is valid and `current-uuid` is the same on all three.

**Additional context**

linstor-csi restores on one node on purpose and then autoplaces the rest. See `reconcileSnapshotResources` in `pkg/client/linstor.go` at v1.11.2, which calls `RestoreSnapshot` with `Nodes: []string{selectedNode}`, followed by `reconcileResourcePlacement`.

LINSTOR creates the autoplaced replicas as brand new volumes. In the satellite's `DrbdLayer.createMetaData` (v1.33.3) a new replica either wins the initial UpToDate race and gets a random current UUID, or asks `DrbdLayerUtils.skipInitSync`. That one returns true for any ZFS or ZFS_THIN volume unless `DrbdOptions/ForceInitialSyncPermanent` is set. For a resource definition that already holds data this shortcut is wrong, the new replica has to sync from the restored one.

A possible mitigation, not tested yet: set `DrbdOptions/ForceInitialSync=true` on the resource group. The controller copies it into `ForceInitialSyncPermanent` when it creates a resource (`CtrlRscCrtApiHelper.copyForceInitialSyncProp`), and then `skipInitSync` returns false. The price is a full initial sync for every new ZFS volume, so it needs measuring before it goes into platform defaults. Restoring on every node that has the snapshot would avoid the empty replicas too.

I'm preparing an upstream report for LINSTOR and will link it here.
